items.t: Replit is no longer working with Anthropic, CEO says
items.d: Over the weekend, Masad clarified that OpenAI would replace Anthropic as its default model provider. Claude will still be available to customers on the platform.
items.x:
Over the weekend, Masad clarified that OpenAI would replace Anthropic as its default model provider. Claude will still be available to customers on the platform.
Replit, the AI coding platform that has become a favorite of startup founders and developers, is no longer working with Anthropic, the company’s CEO and co-founder Amjad Masad said Thursday while onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt.
Masad said the decision was made for a number of different reasons, including cost. Replit announced a partnership with OpenAI in August, but there was never any indication that it was no longer partnering with Anthropic.
“I think ChatGPT is better now,” Masad said, adding that the company uses an internal benchmark to help assess metrics like performance. “We publish a public benchmark as well, and consistently, Sol and Astra perform better on building vibe-coded applications from scratch. It was a decision based on both cost, partnership, and performance.

China’s proposed export bans and controls of artificial intelligence technologies aim to tighten Beijing’s grip in the strategically vital sector, casting a cloud over the commercial prospects of domestic model developers in the global AI race, analysts say.

items.t: DeepSeek: DeepSeek v4.1 Flash 1017
items.d: Article URL: https://openrouter.ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50129121 Points: 511 # Comments: 5
items.x:
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is the October 17, 2026 snapshot of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, served by DeepSeek under the `deepseek-flash` API model name.
It is suited for coding, terminal, and computer-use agents, along with long-horizon tasks that must run to completion across many steps and long-context analysis. Compressed KV caching cuts cache memory to roughly a quarter of the previous Flash generation, significantly reducing costs on agentic workloads. DeepSeek positions it as the cost-efficient tier of the V4.1 family and reports that it exceeds V4 ProOpens in new tab on performance, speed, and task completion time.
This model is hosted by one provider. OpenRouter forwards every request to it directly — no routing decisions to make.
The average price customers actually pay for this model, next to the prices providers post. Caching and discounts mean the price actually paid is often well below the listed one.
Throughput is how fast the model writes (tokens per second — higher is better). Latency is total round-trip time (lower is better). TTFT is time-to-first-token — how long before you see anything appear (lower is better).
Uptime is the percentage of the past 3 days that at least one provider was responding to requests.

items.d: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news261017/ https://openrouter.ai/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50129045 Points: 501 # Comments: 479

For production use, we additionally release deepseek-recipe, a set of Rust libraries with Python bindings that provides the same prompt format as a maintained, protocol-aware toolkit.

items.t: China Meteorological Administration Puts Fengqing AI Ensemble Forecast System Into Operation
items.d: Fengqing Ensemble V1.0 passed operational review at the National Meteorological Centre, with an 11-day effective forecast range for global 500 hPa height in independent tests.
items.x:
The China Meteorological Administration (CMA) has put an AI-based global ensemble forecasting system into national operational use. The Fengqing artificial intelligence global short- and medium-range ensemble weather forecast system, designated CMA-AIM-GFS-Fengqing-ENS-V1.0, recently passed an operational review held at the National Meteorological Centre, according to Chinese-language reports from China Science Daily and IT Home.
The new system should not be confused with the original Fengqing model. That earlier version, developed by the National Meteorological Centre with Tsinghua University in 2024, is a deterministic model that produces a single forecast run. According to a paper in a CMA journal, it has about 3 billion parameters and generates 15-day global forecasts at 25-kilometer resolution in roughly three minutes. The new release is an ensemble system: it produces many forecast members to describe the uncertainty in atmospheric motion, which is the basis for probability forecasts of heavy rain, typhoons and severe convection.
The National Meteorological Centre led development together with the Xiong'an Meteorological Artificial Intelligence Innovation Institute, the National Meteorological Information Centre and Sugon.

items.t: Purple Mountain Laboratories and China Mobile Launch AXP Agent Interconnection Platform
items.d: Built on deterministic networking, AXP is designed to register a million AI agents and run 100,000 at once, with cross-region agent addressing over 4,000 kilometers on the CENI testbed.
items.x:
Purple Mountain Laboratories has launched AXP, a platform for connecting AI agents that runs on deterministic networking. The platform was unveiled on October 16 at the 10th Future Network Development Conference in Nanjing and was developed with China Mobile, Jiangsu Future Network Group and the Jiangsu Future Networks Innovation Institute. The developers describe it as the industry's first agent interconnection platform built on deterministic networking, a claim that has not been independently verified.
Deterministic networking refers to a network's ability to guarantee bounded, predictable delivery for the traffic it carries within a domain, rather than the best-effort behavior of ordinary internet links. AXP applies that idea to the growing number of software agents that need to find and call one another across organizations and regions.
According to the announcement, the platform supports registration of up to a million agents and 100,000 running at the same time.

items.t: DeepSeek Harness v0.2.1-rc1 Arrives as an Unannounced V4.1 Flash Snapshot Briefly Surfaces
items.d: The first 0.2.1 release candidate adds custom plugin indexes, agent-built plugins and per-model reasoning settings. A 'deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017' API entry appeared and was removed.
items.x:
DeepSeek published DeepSeek Harness v0.2.1-rc1 on October 17, the first release candidate of the 0.2.1 series for its open-source agent runtime. The release notes on GitHub bundle the main user- and developer-facing changes made since v0.2.0-rc.2. Several of them, including reasoning-trace translation, the Git Worktrees plugin and the Claude Code Mods compatibility layer, already shipped in the alpha.1 and alpha.2 pre-releases that Pandaily covered earlier. This article focuses on what is new relative to alpha.2.
The biggest addition is around plugins. Users can now discover and install plugins from custom plugin index sources rather than only the official list. The plugin manager gains a 'let the Agent create a plugin' entry that keeps a draft in a creation mode and only starts work once the user sends a request. Enabling, disabling, uninstalling and updating plugins now syncs dependencies, and when hot reload is on, an updated or reinstalled replaceable plugin takes effect immediately; otherwise the app prompts for a restart. Optional plugins support a minimal mode, and the official list can install Claude Code and Codex bundles matched to the current release for headless, SDK and ACP profiles.

items.t: Shanghai AI Laboratory Releases Atria Dawn Full Version With a 512K Context Window
items.d: The agent model built on a 744B MoE GLM-5.2 base moves past its September preview with higher scores on JobBench, WideSearch and PaperBench. Full weights are still marked 'Coming soon'.
items.x:
Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory has released the full version of Atria Dawn, its agent-oriented large model, about a month after the Atria Dawn Preview appeared in mid-September. The model is trained on the 744-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts GLM-5.2 base and targets research and engineering work that requires understanding an environment, calling tools and completing multi-step tasks.
The headline change in the lab's announcement is the context window, which grows to 512K tokens from the 256K offered by the preview. The model download table in the project's GitHub repository still lists 256K for both the full model and its FP8 version, so developers may want to check the hosted API documentation for the limit that applies.
The lab now frames the model's abilities in four categories. Discovery covers gathering and organizing evidence, deep research and turning research questions into executable experiment plans. Creation covers building software, interactive applications, games, data visualizations and machine-learning systems. Delivery turns documents, data and design requirements into reports, slide decks and other structured outputs.

items.t: Rokid and Tencent Mobility Bring Voice Ride-Hailing to AI Glasses via Agent-to-Agent Link
items.d: Users say a destination and the glasses handle pickup points, fare comparison, booking and password-free payment, with car details shown in view while they wait.
items.x:
Rokid has launched ride-hailing on its AI glasses in partnership with Tencent Mobility, letting wearers book a car by voice without taking out a phone. Rokid describes it as the industry's first native ride-hailing service for AI glasses, a claim made by the company.
Once the Tencent Mobility agent is connected, a user only needs to say where they want to go. The glasses then handle the full flow: understanding the request, suggesting pickup and drop-off points, checking nearby cars, estimating fares and comparing vehicle types, placing the order and paying the fare. While the user waits, the license plate, car details and estimated arrival time are shown in their field of view, with voice reminders. According to Chinese tech outlet Leikeji, Android and iOS users need to update the Rokid AI app to version 1.15 to use the feature.
The integration works as a split between two agents. Rokid's glasses agent handles understanding the user, conversation and on-lens display. Tencent Mobility's agent provides the ride-hailing service. The two connect directly over the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol.

items.t: Tencent Hunyuan Open-Sources Hy Memory 2.0, Adding Working and Code Memory for AI Agents
items.d: The release spans an SDK, a 30B-A3B memory model and the MemHub local app. Tencent reports 72.6% on LoCoMo while cutting tokens per question from 1,159 to 703.
items.x:
Tencent Hunyuan has released version 2.0 of Hy Memory, its memory framework for AI agents, and open-sourced all three layers of the stack: a dedicated memory model, the framework itself and a local memory app called MemHub. The layers can be used separately or combined. Tencent says Hy Memory is already used by internal teams in finance, news, knowledge management, office agents, social entertainment and games.
The framework handles storage, updating and evolution of three memory types: chat, working and code. Developers connect it to agents through an SDK, published on PyPI as hy-memory 2.0.2. Working memory and code memory are new in 2.0. They record a task's goal, decisions already made, intermediate results and reusable lessons along with the conditions under which those lessons apply. Before resuming a long-running task, the system first works out which task is in progress, then retrieves relevant decisions, still-valid experience and prior work history. Chat memory now groups scattered facts into events with time, place and people, merging duplicates and resolving conflicts before passing context to the model.
Tencent reports first place against open-source frameworks including Mem0, MemOS and EverOS on four benchmarks.

items.t: DeepSeek Adds Standalone Search and Fetch APIs for Agents, Priced at 5 Yuan per 1,000 Calls
items.d: The new endpoints return structured web results or a page as Markdown. Each costs 5 yuan per 1,000 successful requests and is capped at 5 queries per second per account.
items.x:
DeepSeek has added two standalone tools to its API platform: a Search endpoint that queries the web and returns structured results, and a Fetch endpoint that retrieves a single page and returns its content as Markdown. According to the company's Chinese-language API documentation, the tools are meant to give agent and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications access to live web content without a separate third-party search provider.
Both are raw JSON APIs that use the same Bearer authentication as the rest of the DeepSeek API. Search is served at api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search and Fetch at api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/fetch.
A Search request takes a query of up to 128 characters and can return between 1 and 50 results, with 10 as the default. Developers can pass the user's original question to help the service read intent, supply an IP address to favor localized results, and ask for full page text. Queries accept operators including site: and -site: to include or exclude domains, quoted exact phrases, lang: to restrict languages, and after: and before: to bound publication dates.

items.t: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
items.d: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
items.x:
OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts.
The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own. The incident—which likely would have resulted in criminal charges had they been performed directly by a person—has further heightened concerns that widespread AI use could have harmful effects on an unprecedented scale.
Easier to beg for forgiveness than ask permission
In two of the cases reported Thursday, OpenAI agents tasked with retrieving information from websites hacked them when the models ran into obstacles obtaining it directly.

In the US, cops have vowed to crack down on AI CSAM since at least 2024, when the Department of Justice made one of the earliest arrests . After charging a Wisconsin man with spreading “thousands of realistic images of prepubescent minors” across Telegram and Instagram, the DOJ clarified to law enforcement that “CSAM generated by AI is still CSAM.”

items.t: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
items.d: The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles.
items.x:
The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles.
AI agents from multiple providers accessed personal data and confidential material at Indian organizations during research and testing, India’s cybersecurity agency said Thursday.
The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said it had received “multiple voluntary disclosures from AI model providers” whose models, during research and evaluation runs on the open internet, “had reached the live systems of Indian organizations.”
This makes India the latest stop on what has become a world tour for rogue AI agents. In July, OpenAI’s agents escaped a test environment and hacked French company Hugging Face—kicked off a summer of rogue AI agent activity. Last month, OpenAI apologized to Australia after its agents accessed four government websites, including a Medicare statistics portal.
At Hugging Face, OpenAI’s agents started the same way but then found and exploited software flaws to run code on the company’s servers.

items.x:
Techable VC founder and former Nvidia exec Amulya Vishwanath tells Equity why robotics’ ChatGPT moment can wait, and why the real opportunity is rebuilding its basic building blocks.
Amulya Vishwanath, who spent seven years leading product marketing for NVIDIA’s robotics platforms, says robotics is currently in its “Lego era,” with the basic building blocks like actuators, robotic hands, software, and safety standards still being rebuilt.
This view runs counter to those who believe that robotics, powered by a general foundation model, is about to have its “ChatGPT moment” — that day when the shockingly capable chatbot was launched in late 2022. (General Intuition CEO Pim de Witte told Equity earlier this year that a single general foundation model would make much of today’s specialized robotics work redundant, and be that moment.)
On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Dominic-Madori Davis caught up with Vishwanath to discuss where she’s writing first checks as the founder and managing partner of Techable VC.

according to Elorian's evaluations, Glimpse outperforms even GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning, with competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks.
Elorian, the Palo Alto AI startup that raised a $55 million seed round at a $300 million valuation before it launched a product, released its first model on Friday, TechCrunch has exclusively learned.
The model, Glimpse, is launching as a research preview with API access and a chat interface is waitlist-only, so for now it’s a results table and a thesis. The thesis? Today’s AI models, for all their skill with language and code, still can’t really see.
Most multimodal models look at an image once, convert it to tokens, and then reason about it in text — like describing a photo from memory. Glimpse keeps going back to the source.

items.t: Meta may use sweeping new commercial TOS to avoid millions in AI licensing fees
items.d: Meta “streamlined” its commercial TOS. Legal experts warn it’s an AI power grab.
items.x:
Legal experts are sounding alarms that Meta will soon update its commercial terms to require business accounts to allow Meta to train AI on their linked website content, not just their social media posts.
Kicking in on October 30, the TOS update won’t allow businesses to opt out, instead suggesting that businesses stop using Meta services if they won’t agree to let Meta bots freely crawl their linked content.
As Nieman Lab reported Thursday, this will affect all business accounts but is particularly shocking for news publishers who could perhaps charge Meta millions in licensing fees to continually access their articles for AI training. Currently news organizations are fighting a battle with OpenAI over whether such training without licensing is fair use, and Meta's terms seemingly risk granting it sweeping permissions, no matter which way the court leans.

items.t: Jev is Vercel’s fastest-adopted AI model ever
items.d: The data comes from Vercel's AI gateway, a unified API service similar to OpenRouter.
items.x:
The data comes from the Vercel's AI gateway, a unified API service similar to OpenRouter.
Jev has become the fastest adopted AI model ever — at least by some measures.
Vercel data published on Thursday shows that, within two weeks of its launch, the buzzy decision model was being used by 35% of paid teams, with nearly double the reach of the second most popular model, Sonnet 5.5. It’s the fastest adoption a model has ever seen in its first two weeks, according to Vercel’s data, and a major accomplishment for the model’s creators, Typesafe AI.
Published in limited release on September 15, Jev is designed as a lightweight tool for choosing between a few pre-determined outputs. Limiting the outputs lets the model run cheaper and faster than alternatives like Sonnet, making it ideal for classifying large quantities of data quickly. That new approach has attracted significant buzz in the weeks since Jev’s release — inspiring competing offerings from OpenAI and Amazon, among others — but until now there has been little hard data to back up the good vibes.
The data comes from the Vercel’s AI gateway, a unified API service similar to OpenRouter.

items.t: While Software Ate the World, This Company Ate Its Own Software Business
items.d: Editor’s note: This article is republished from Jumpstart, a TechNode Group publication. In 2023, AI software was DataCanvas’s business. By the first half of 2026, it was almost absent from its sales. The change is unusually stark. AI…
items.x:
Editor’s note: This article is republished from Jumpstart , a TechNode Group publication.
In 2023, AI software was DataCanvas’s business. By the first half of 2026, it was almost absent from its sales.
The change is unusually stark. AI foundational software services generated 76.5% of the Chinese company’s revenue in 2023. Three years later, their contribution had fallen to 0.1%.
This was more than an old division being overshadowed by a faster-growing one. Software-service revenue itself contracted—from RMB81.3 million in 2023 to less than RMB500,000 in the first six months of 2026. Meanwhile, total annual revenue climbed from RMB106.2 million in 2023 to RMB1.10 billion in 2025, a compound annual growth rate of 221.5%.
DataCanvas had built a different business.
The Beijing company, known in China as 九章云极, began redirecting its resources toward computing infrastructure in early 2023. It subsequently added cloud services, turning from a supplier of software tools into a company that helps assemble computing infrastructure and sells access to its capacity.
On September 29, 2026, it filed for a Hong Kong listing .

items.t: Mark Wahlberg on using AI in film ‘the right way’ and being open to an AI clone carrying on his legacy
items.d: Actor and angel investor Mark Wahlberg says he's OK with using AI in filmmaking, provided it's used "to enhance what you're doing."
items.x:
Actor and angel investor Mark Wahlberg says he's OK with using AI in filmmaking, provided it's used "to enhance what you're doing."
Even as Hollywood remains divided over the use of AI in filmmaking, actor and director Mark Wahlberg believes the technology has a place in the industry as long as it’s used the right way.
Wahlberg, who’s also an entrepreneur and angel investor, took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt to share his perspective on AI’s role in filmmaking, and how he’s open to having an AI likeness of himself carry on his legacy.
The actor said he plans to potentially use AI to enhance certain aspects of the upcoming Pete Rose biopic, in which he’ll star in the title role.
“It’s a fairly expensive movie, but, we’re talking about utilizing [AI] to enhance the stadium setting, things of that nature,” Wahlberg said. “I don’t think you should just, you know, put an idea into ChatGPT and it puts out a script, and then you should go make that and not use real actors. But if you can use it to enhance what you’re doing, I’m all for that.”
That said, Wahlberg made special mention of his belief that storytelling should remain at the heart of filmmaking.
“I’ve done big, effects-driven movies,” Wahlberg said.

items.t: Veritas expands its anti-counterfeit chip to jewelry, trophies, and fragrance bottles

items.x:
Counterfeits of luxury goods are a major problem for fashion houses. Counterfeiters are getting better at replicating brands' marks and passing off dupes,
Veritas was founded by Luci Holland, a former Tesla technical product manager who also has a background in design and art. Its chip is built to be easily inserted into products without damaging them. Brands can use it to verify whether a product is the real deal, and customers can show a certificate of ownership through the company’s app.
Holland said other approaches are easier to defeat, because a digital record can be reproduced through a copied QR code or static NFC link.
“Our approach combines secure, authenticated chip responses with integration into the product itself. Our chip generates a secure response with each tap and includes a tamper-detection wire.

items.t: Super Scam Me documentary shows what it takes to catch a romance scammer

items.x:
If you got a DM from an unverified Jon Bon Jovi account after commenting on one of his official Instagram posts, what would it take to make you believe it was really the rock star hoping to connect? And at what point when he starts asking you to send money—like lose-your-house kind of money—would you snap out of the fantasy and stop draining your bank account?
In a documentary premiering Saturday— Super Scam Me —investigative journalist Mariana van Zeller goes deep into this toxic love-bombing terrain. In a clip that Ars is exclusively debuting below, you can see how van Zeller worked with an ethical hacker, Arman the Cyber, to use a fake bitcoin receipt and bait the fake Bon Jovi, giving the victim some much-needed closure.
Sneak peek at National Geographic's Super Scam Me .
Broadcasting on National Geographic at 9 pm ET and available to stream on Disney+ and Hulu, the documentary takes viewers on an empathetic quest to understand how the line between “lover” and “fraud victim” gets blurred in romance scams that the Federal Trade Commission says cost Americans nearly $1.5 billion in losses each year.

items.t: Benn Jordan on Flock, privacy, and the new surveillance backlash
items.d: Today, I’m talking with Benn Jordan, musician, YouTuber, researcher, and investigative journalist. You might know Benn from those first two titles — he’s got a prolific discography of experimental music dating back decades. But in the last…
items.x:
Today, I’m talking with Benn Jordan, musician, YouTuber, researcher, and investigative journalist. You might know Benn from those first two titles — he’s got a prolific discography of experimental music dating back decades.
But in the last couple of years, he’s become a high-profile face in the creator and media spaces for his work investigating Flock Safety, the maker of automatic license plate readers and the software that powers them.
Benn recently testified in front of Congress , at a hearing the Senate Judiciary Committee’s Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism held, dedicated to Flock and other ALPR systems. This hearing felt like the culmination of months and months of growing criticism and bipartisan backlash against Flock — all of which is taking a shape similar to the pushback against AI data centers.
This has led to major fallout for Flock. Hundreds of cities, counties, and other local governments have begun canceling contracts , and Flock is now under investigation by Republican Sen. Josh Hawley.

Replit CEO Amjad Masad envisions a future of “self-driving companies,” where AI agents handle day-to-day tasks and people focus on higher-level decisions.
Replit CEO and co-founder, Amjad Masad, has seen how AI is impacting the workplace first-hand, with businesses adopting his company’s AI coding tools to develop and launch their own software. At TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco on Thursday, Masad shared what Replit has learned about what that means for the future of work in the AI age, including how humans will still play key roles as AI agents come to work alongside them.
He described his vision of a “self-driving company,” referring not to robotaxi makers, but how agents will come to do much of the grunt work at companies while people become more valued for their judgement and taste.
“The reality is, all of our jobs — perhaps everyone in this audience, especially — changed over the past year,” he said, addressing the audience at Disrupt.

items.t: Kling AI 4.0 suggests a shift in AI video competition from visual quality to directorial control
items.d: AI video generation is no longer just about producing a visually impressive clip. For creators looking to use AI to make short films, advertisements or even feature films, the harder questions are whether characters can remain consistent…
items.x:
Kling AI’s latest release, Kling 4.0, introduces features designed to tackle these challenges. The model update focuses on motion performance, creative control and longer-form storytelling.
Kling 4.0 supports native video generation of up to 30 seconds in a single generation, along with up to 15 multimodal reference assets and 10 keyframes, giving creators more control over characters, scenes, actions and camera movements. Rather than focusing solely on visual quality, these features reflect a broader effort to make AI video generation more consistent and easier to control.
Screenshot from videos generated by Kling 4.0
From generating images to directing shots
AI video creation has traditionally relied heavily on text prompts. Creators describe the scenes they want, and the model generates the footage. However, complex camera movements, character actions and scene transitions can be difficult to control precisely. Even when individual shots look convincing, combining them can result in inconsistent character appearances or discontinuous actions.
Kling 4.0’s multimodal reference feature supports images, videos and audio as inputs, with up to 15 reference assets.

The company has used robotic refueling as an initial commercial application, testing an explosion-protected system at a station in Foshan. It plans to use the funding to improve its robot AI, collect operational data from real-world deployments and expand commercialization. [ 36Kr , in Chinese]

Ant Group has released the weights of Ling-3.1-flash, making its AI model available for developers to deploy on their own infrastructure. The model has approximately 560 billion total parameters, activates about 25 billion per token and supports a context window of up to one million tokens.
The release follows the model’s earlier introduction and includes deployment support through inference frameworks such as SGLang and vLLM. It targets coding, agent workflows and professional tasks that require processing long documents and interacting with external tools.
The team has also developed a mixed-precision deployment approach that reduces model-weight memory requirements from approximately 534GB to 292GB. In its reported Hopper GPU configuration, this reduced the deployment requirement from eight GPUs to four. [ Ant Group ]

Xiaomi has open-sourced MiDashengLM-Spatial, an audio-language model that combines general sound understanding with spatial awareness. The company released model weights and inference code under the Apache 2.0 license.
Built on Xiaomi’s MiDashengLM audio model, the system processes binaural audio to identify sound sources and reason about their positions and spatial relationships. It retains capabilities such as speech recognition, audio captioning and questions about environmental sounds and music.
Xiaomi plans to bring the technology to smart-home products and vehicle cabins, enabling devices to respond to both what they hear and where the sound originates. The release extends its Dasheng audio-model series beyond recognizing sound content to understanding the surrounding acoustic environment. [ Xiaomi ]

items.t: 4Paradigm and RiseUnion Open-Source ModelSphere for Heterogeneous LLM Serving
items.d: ModelSphere unifies cluster serving, KV caching and AutoTune under Apache 2.0, with claimed support for Ascend, Iluvatar, Moore Threads and Hygon DCU.
items.x:
4Paradigm and RiseUnion have open-sourced ModelSphere, a production-oriented AI deployment platform that unifies compute management, model serving and runtime tuning under the Apache 2.0 license. The code is published on GitHub at modelsphere/modelsphere, which lists an Apache-2.0 license and was pushed again on the launch day.
The companies say ModelSphere sits above engines such as vLLM and SGLang: those stacks squeeze more work from a single server, while ModelSphere handles cluster routing, a shared KV cache pool, quality-of-service autoscaling, hang recovery and online AutoTune. Built-in features listed in the joint announcement include a graphical deploy panel, elastic scale-out, prefill-decode split serving, three-level KV caching, high-availability load balancing and automatic resume after a service break.
Heterogeneous chips are a stated focus. Through an EngineX inference layer, ModelSphere is said to schedule Huawei Ascend, Iluvatar, Moore Threads and Hygon DCU resources in one fleet so teams do not rewrite low-level code for each accelerator.

items.t: Kling 4.0 Goes Fully Live on klingai.com With Audio, MCP and CLI Hooks

items.x:
Kuaishou's Kling AI says Kling 4.0 is now fully available on klingai.com, moving the model from preview access to a general rollout. The update focuses on longer native clips, richer multi-reference control and audio that ships with the picture, rather than rehashing the September capability preview.
Creators can generate a single native clip of up to 30 seconds and set as many as 10 keyframes to steer character state, scene changes and plot beats. A generation job can combine up to 10 images, five video clips and seven subjects so references for character, motion, camera and sound work together. The product also supports multi-shot continuation that can extend a sequence toward about two minutes.
Audio is part of the full launch package. Kling 4.0 supports dual-channel stereo and lip sync across multiple languages and regional accents, including Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French and Hindi, plus several Chinese dialects and English accent variants.

items.t: Axera Unveils AX8860 Edge AI Chip Series With 256 TOPS and Up to 128 GB Memory
items.d: At CIIF 2026, Axera launched the 6nm AX8860 for on-site large-model inference, with AXLink cascading, PCIe 5.0 and a vLLM/SGLang-friendly toolchain.
items.x:
Axera has unveiled the AX8860, a 6-nanometer edge AI chip series aimed at running large models on factory floors, warehouses and robots rather than in distant data centers. The company presented the line at CIIF 2026 in Shanghai and framed it as a compute base for physical AI that must sense, decide and act on site.
According to Axera's official release, the AX8860 delivers up to 256 TOPS of mixed-precision compute with native FP4 support, up to 273 GB/s of memory bandwidth and as much as 128 GB of LPDDR5X. It supports Axera's AXLink multi-chip cascading and PCIe 5.0 for scaling, plus 64-channel video decode and 16-channel encode for multi-camera vision workloads.
Around the chip, Axera also showed the Yuanxi A256S module and related inference cards and servers. The software stack is meant to look familiar to cloud developers: the company says the series supports vLLM, SGLang and PyTorch and offers an OpenAI API-compatible service interface, with tools covering quantization, conversion, compilation, profiling and debugging.
Partner channel claims have drawn attention beyond the official brief.

Editor’s note: This article was written by Lucia, a TechNode reporter.
Physical AI is moving beyond pre-programmed robots toward systems that can understand, decide, and adapt. But unlike digital AI, which can learn from vast amounts of online data, physical AI faces a shortage of real-world data needed to train models and improve robotic capabilities.
What happened: At its Kosmo AI Day in Shanghai on Oct. 14, Hesai launched Kosmo, a 3D world data engine designed to transform physical environments into high-fidelity 3D digital spaces for robot training, world model development and immersive content creation.
Why it matters: Kosmo is positioned as data infrastructure for Physical AI, addressing the challenge of obtaining real-world data that is accurate, affordable and available at scale.
A robot demonstrated how Kosmo, held in its hand, scanned a space.
How it works: Kosmo captures real spaces with lidar, imaging and motion data, then turns them into 3D scenes with AI-generated completion and object labeling.
Kosmo adapts scenes for robot simulation and can generate over 10,000 training trajectories from a single capture.

items.t: Hesai Launches Kosmo, a 3D World Data Engine With an 8K AI Spatial Camera
items.d: Lidar maker Hesai launched Kosmo, pairing the Kosmo One 8K AI spatial camera with the Kosmo World cloud platform to turn real spaces into 3D assets for robot training and world models.
items.x:
Hesai, a lidar company known for automotive sensors, has launched Kosmo, a 3D world data engine aimed at one of Physical AI's persistent bottlenecks: high-quality real-world data at scale. The stack pairs Kosmo One, which Hesai calls the world's first 8K ultra HD AI spatial camera, with the Kosmo World cloud platform to turn physical spaces into high-fidelity 3D digital environments for robot training, world-model development and immersive content.
Kosmo One combines high-resolution lidar, a one-inch imaging sensor and a high-precision inertial measurement unit (IMU). Hesai says the sensors stay synchronized at the microsecond level so the device captures geometry, color, texture and camera pose together. Reconstruction uses 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), which the company says can reach millimeter-level geometric accuracy and reproduce materials, lighting and shadows. A single operator can scan a typical 100-square-meter indoor space in about 15 minutes, according to Hesai, and Kosmo World then builds 3D models at speeds the company puts at up to roughly five times those of comparable products. Hesai notes that "8K" refers to maximum capture resolution, while exported files top out at 6K.
Kosmo World is powered by Hesai's Kosmo Spatial Core (KSC).

items.t: Working at the frontier shapes expectations for the future
items.d: Working at the frontier shapes expectations for the future
items.x:
We’re sharing two reports: the first covers how AI is changing employment inside Anthropic, and the second looks at the gap between how the public and Anthropic employees expect AI to affect work and the economy.
Anthropic staff and US workers don’t seem to have different theories about how AI affects jobs. Instead, they have different experiences of what AI capabilities are. Those different experiences seem closely related to perceptions about what will happen to work in the future.
Anthropic is a company at the frontier of AI adoption, and that adoption has changed the way we hire. We find that over the past year, we're hiring for a smaller share of junior positions, and a smaller share of our employees work in technical roles. At the same time, the rate of hours worked by AI agents has shot up. By March 2026, agents worked more hours than employees. By August, there were six times more agents than employees at Anthropic, and productivity increased.
That’s led to Anthropic producing more code per person, but that’s a notoriously imperfect measure. We see signs of increased productivity elsewhere: we’ve closed more sales per sales representative, and processed more contracts.

items.t: How employment is changing at Anthropic
items.d: How employment is changing at Anthropic
items.x:
How has AI restructured work and employment at Anthropic? As a company at the frontier of AI adoption, Anthropic could be a leading indicator of how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy.
What transformations of work and employment can we expect under increasingly powerful AI? Anthropic is worth studying because it has thoroughly molded its workflows around AI. Agents flit through Slack chats and schedule meetings. They autonomously fix bugs and collectively tackle huge engineering projects. Agent hours worked outnumber human hours 6 to 1. Changes happening at Anthropic now give advanced signals about a possible future of work and employment.
This report draws on comprehensive internal Anthropic data covering employment, AI use, output metrics, employee surveys, internal communication patterns, employee calendar data, and hiring decision records. It contextualizes these quantitative data with 17 employee interviews.
We find that even as the company grows, relative hiring in junior technical positions has slowed. Productivity for both engineers and non-technical employees has leapt up and did so sharply when they adopted coding agents.

items.t: Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins
items.d: Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins
items.x:
The decades-old mystery of the origins of one of the most popular cryptographic standards has been explained.
“It’s just timestamps”: the decades-old mystery of the origins of one of the most popular cryptographic standards has been explained.
We pursued this long-standing open question of the cryptographic community to settle concerns about ECDSA, which is one of our most widely used cryptographic standards.
Readers should take this as a fun closing chapter and the end of years of speculation. There is no action to be taken or things to do differently. Most researchers trusted the curves already. Enjoy.
ECDSA is the most widely used elliptic curve cryptography standard. It was adopted by NIST in 2000 as part of the FIPS 186-2 Digital Signature Standard which lists a set of standard elliptic curves of varying sizes and security levels. For curves over prime and binary fields, the specifications published a “seed” parameter whose hash value is used to define the coefficient b of the curve. The provenance of these seeds has been a long-standing question, as they were provided by the NSA with no explanation or justification.

items.t: Designing more efficient quantum circuits with Claude
items.d: Designing more efficient quantum circuits with Claude
items.x:
Working largely on its own, Claude designed quantum circuits that improve on the best published versions, in some cases by an order of magnitude or more.
Quantum computers will need carefully designed circuits to run useful algorithms on limited hardware. We gave Claude plain-language specifications for eight such circuits, drawn from chemistry, optimization, physics simulation, and number theory, along with an automated evaluator that checks and scores each design. Working largely on its own, Claude found designs that improve on the best published circuits, in some cases by an order of magnitude or more. Such improvements substantially reduce the quantum resources that useful applications require, so practical quantum computers could arrive sooner than previously anticipated.
This work was led by Andi Gu as part of Anthropic’s STEM Fellows Program, with mentorship from Alek Kemeny, a quantum physicist at Anthropic, in collaboration with Susanne Yelin (Harvard University) and Mikhail Lukin (Harvard University and QuEra Computing).

items.t: The AI expectations gap
items.d: The AI expectations gap
items.x:
How will AI reshape the economy in the years ahead? What is the core source of disagreement about AI's future impact on the economy? This note presents new survey evidence on these questions.
Szymon Sacher, Tess Cotter, Charles I. Jones, Anton Korinek, Peter McCrory
What is the core source of disagreement about AI's future impact on the economy? Is it principally due to differences in beliefs about how quickly AI capabilities will improve? Or does it reflect disagreement about how quickly and in what form those capabilities translate to real-world adoption? Which views on the future path of AI are consistent with rapid economic growth?
This note presents new survey evidence on these questions. In August 2026, we surveyed two groups: a sample of US adults that was nationally representative and Anthropic staff.1 The questions covered, among other things, AI’s capabilities, how widely it will be used, how much time it saves, how autonomous it will be, and how difficult it will be for a displaced worker to find a job in a different occupation.2 Anthropic staff build and use frontier AI every day. The second survey therefore shows how people closest to the technology anticipate its future, both in capabilities and in broader economic impact.
We report the following main findings.

items.t: How the Claude Code team does code review
items.d: How do you review code at the volume agents produce it? The Claude Code team shares its review process, from Claude verifying its own work to risk-tiered human approval, plus a checklist for adopting it.
items.x:
How do you review code at the volume agents produce it? On the Claude Code team, once we had high coverage and deep reviews, we started optimizing for the minimum amount of human review time that doesn't raise reverts or incidents.
We've said before that Claude writes about 90 percent of Claude Code's own code. So how do we review code at the volume we produce it? Does anyone read code anymore? And if something breaks, who catches it?
This post covers the code review flow on the Claude Code team and how it has evolved. From June to September, merged pull requests to Claude Code's codebase more than doubled while the share that had to be reverted fell by more than 40 percent.
We didn't remove review. But we did move most of the reading to machines, optimized for human time and attention, and invested heavily in making it fast and easy to undo mistakes.
When agents write code, the number of changes goes up, fast. In Anthropic's monorepo, changes landing per day went from about 2,500 in May to more than 30,000 in September this year.
Claude Code lives in its own repository, separate from the monorepo, but it's seeing a lot of pressure too.

items.t: How an Anthropic Japan BDR runs his day with a fleet of Claude agents
items.d: How one business development representative clears his inbound queue and drafts bilingual customer emails with Claude Managed Agents and Claude Tag.
items.x:
How one business development representative clears his inbound queue and drafts bilingual customer emails with Claude Managed Agents and Claude Tag.
As a business development representative on Anthropic's Japan team, my job is to show Japanese companies how Claude can simplify and automate their workflows, but until earlier this year, most of mine were still manual. I was spending a couple of hours each morning routing and qualifying leads, then writing emails in Japanese or English. In the time I had left, I was updating our CRM, often a day or more behind. Now my agents prepare most of that before my day starts, and I review it.
The first Claude-run workflow I built was pretty scrappy, but it did the job. I'd hand Claude one piece of my work at a time, correct what it got wrong, and save those corrections. Over time, that grew into a handful of agents, each covering a different routine.
Word got around quickly, and teammates started asking for my prompts and skills so they could build their own. All I could send them was a zip file with my skills and a few Markdown files from the knowledge base, which they had to upload to Claude and then answer a round of setup questions before anything worked. My own setup was getting harder to keep track of, too.

The company generated over $30 million in revenue in two years and was acquired by MyFitness for an undisclosed amount of money in March.
Zach Yadegari has enjoyed an immense amount of success for someone who only recently graduated from high school. Founder of the AI-fueled calorie tracking app Cal AI, Yadegari is only 19, but his company has rocketed to viral fame over the past two years. At TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday, Yadegari shared details of that surprising rise to prominence.
Cal AI, which was founded in 2024, exploded its presence on the internet thanks largely to Yadegari’s strategy of deploying a small army of influencers to promote the brand. The company generated over $30 million in revenue in two years and was acquired by MyFitness for an undisclosed amount of money in March.
Discussing his social strategy onstage, Yadegari noted that an early sign of success came when an influencer’s post about them led to approximately a thousand new users over the course of two days.
“From there, we figured out, okay, this can actually work for us, and so we started recruiting influencers as fast as we could — paying as many people as possible to start posting for us,” he said. “What we saw was that it was a clear formula. It was pretty linear, but it was extremely fast.

أعلنت شركة أمازون إطلاق جهازين جديدين من أجهزة Bee القابلة للارتداء، المدعومة بالذكاء الاصطناعي، مع اشتراك مأجور يتيح مزايا إضافية، أبرزها التكامل مع خدمات أمازون والمساعد الصوتي Alexa Plus، لاقتراح المنتجات وتنفيذ مهام يومية استنادًا إلى محادثات المستخدم.
وتأتي الخطوة بعد استحواذ أمازون العام الماضي على شركة Bee الناشئة، التي طوّرت جهازًا صغيرًا يستمع إلى المحادثات اليومية ويلخصها، في مسعى لتوسيع حضور الشركة في سوق الأجهزة الشخصية المدعومة بالذكاء الاصطناعي.
وتضم المجموعة الجديدة جهاز Bee Frontier بسعر قدره 75 دولارًا، وهو نسخة مطوّرة من الجهاز الأصلي، بالإضافة إلى Bee Eclipse بسعر قدره 99 دولارًا، وهو يأتي بتصميم مستطيل يشبه بطاقة الائتمان، ويلتصق مغناطيسيًا بالجزء الخلفي من الهاتف الذكي.
ويتوفر Bee Frontier بدءًا من اليوم باللون الأسود والأخضر والبنفسجي، ويمكن ارتداؤه حول المعصم على غرار أساور اللياقة البدنية، أو تثبيته بالملابس باستخدام مشبك.
وأعادت أمازون تصميم زر التسجيل ليصبح أكثر وضوحًا، مع الاحتفاظ بميكروفونين ومؤشر ضوئي للتسجيل وبطارية تدوم نحو سبعة أيام للشحنة الواحدة، بالإضافة إلى مقاومة الماء والغبار وفق معيار IP67.
وأما Bee Eclipse، فتخطط الشركة لطرحه قريبًا بألوان الأسود والوردي والأصفر والفضي.

items.x:
Meta and Apple have teamed up for the launch of the social media giant's newest model, Muse Spark Open, which will run locally on Apple silicon.
Meta has launched what it calls the “most capable” open-weight model in the United States. Dubbed Muse Spark Open, the model also has the distinction of having been designed to work with Macs.
The new model, which leverages 816 billion parameters and a 1 million token context window, claims to offer superior performance to other popular open weight models, according to evaluation results released by Meta on Thursday.
Muse Spark Open is natively multimodal and built for complex coding tasks and agentic labor. It has also been designed to run locally on Apple’s computers. However, you will still need a lot of power to run the model locally, with a requirement of at least 1 terabyte of RAM, per Engadget. The model will run best via the Mac Studio that comes equipped with the M5 Ultra chip.
Still, if you can muster the memory, Muse Spark Open may prove a significant work horse for coding and other desktop tasks.

items.t: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay sees a future where AI devices replace the need to use apps

items.x:
Speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt, Amazon devices chief Panos Panay described a future where ambient AI devices work in the background, anticipating users' needs instead of waiting for commands.
Amazon is placing its bets on ambient computing, not apps, as the future of personal AI.
Alongside the launch of its new AI wearables from Bee, Panos Panay, who serves as Amazon’s SVP of Devices, Alexa & Leo, took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Thursday to talk in more depth about where he sees personal computing headed.
“A lot of times, what you’re doing right now — what we all do right now — is we have to remember what we’re asking our tool to do for us,” Panay began, explaining that this is how we engage with our modern smartphones. “It’s like point, shoot, return,” Panay continued. “I think where we’re headed is a world [that] starts with ambient devices.”
By “ambient devices,” he means those that work quietly in the background, using sensors, and AI to help you figure out what needs to be done, instead of the other way around, where you’re telling the device what you need to do.
“As it works in the background, you’re able to stay more present. You’re able to get more done. You’re about to spend more time with people… you’re not afraid if you miss something.

items.x:
METR will publish its own assessments of Anthropic’s risks, incidents, and practices, and the frontier AI model maker has given up the right to block them.
Anthropic is giving employee-level access to six researchers from METR, a nonprofit that tests frontier AI models, to independently assess Anthropic’s models, safety practices, and risk management, the company said in a blog post on Thursday.
The arrangement comes at a time where incidents of AI agents acting outside their instructions have been disclosed every week or two since late August. The incidents have sharpened calls for independent checks on AI companies.
“We want to be publicly accountable for the decisions we’re making,” Anthropic said in the blog post. “We aim to close the gap between what evaluators understand about a frontier AI company’s systems and what the company itself understands.”
Under the new arrangement, the METR team has Anthropic-issued company laptops, office space, and access to internal tools roughly on par with what Anthropic’s own risk assessment teams use.

Open social network Bluesky is once again expanding beyond its flagship app. At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 on Thursday, the company announced the launch of a new tool that allows creators to make websites, quizzes, games, polls, and other interactive experiences.
The tool is an expansion of Attie, Bluesky’s more experimental platform, which initially offered AI-powered technology for building custom social feeds. With its new creation capabilities, the idea is to allow everyday users to create the kind of experiences that previously only software developers could build.
These user-created games, sites, and other experiences will also live on the same AT Protocol (atproto) that powers Bluesky and other decentralized social apps that make up the decentralized social web known as the Atmosphere.

items.t: Accelerating the search for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity
items.d: Accelerating the search for novel antimicrobial peptides using Google Antigravity for Science.
items.x:
Learn how Google Antigravity provides an agentic science workbench to discover, structurally evaluate, and prioritize novel antimicrobial peptides in hours.
Pengfei Tian, Maxwell L Bileschi, Zoi Tsangalidou, Sukhdeep Singh and Lucy. J. Colwell
New antibiotics are urgently needed to help with rising levels of antimicrobial resistance, but searching for new therapeutics is often a slow, labor-intensive process. With Google Antigravity, our agentic development platform, this process can now be made easier.
Google Antigravity provides an agentic science workbench that empowers biologists to discover, structurally evaluate, and prioritize promising targets quickly, compressing what used to be a fragmented search over multiple databases into a single session. It also helps researchers scan through millions of previously uncharacterized proteins in the UniProt database using ProtNLM, a model that predicts biological function from amino acid sequences.
This technical walkthrough shows how biologists used Google Antigravity to uncover a novel antimicrobial peptide candidate which has predicted activity against the pathogens involved in respiratory tract infections.

items.t: Singer or clanker? YouTube Music will tell you with new gen AI labeling.
items.d: The AI music labels are rolling out now in YouTube Music and will come to YouTube soon.
items.x:
Genuine human creativity takes time, but you know what doesn't? AI slop. There are countless AI models out there that can make something that passes for music, and you might come across those tracks on streaming services without realizing it. Google says it's going to begin labeling that content in YouTube Music, building on similar disclosures in the main YouTube app.
Google is not outright banning AI music or even speaking ill of it. "Generative AI is opening up new ways for artists to create, experiment, and share music," the company says in a blog post.
However, the company also acknowledges that people want to know if a song was created with generative AI tools. A new label for AI content on YouTube Music is now rolling out in the app and on the website, which looks a lot like a label Google began adding to AI-generated videos on YouTube earlier this year.

But it’s not hard to imagine how Rivian might integrate something like Claude, OpenAI’s Dots or Meta’s Muse assistant into its software. The company has developed its in-car software from the ground up, instead of leaning on Apple CarPlay or Android Auto, and built a lot of its own applications, like navigation (though it has worked to integrate popular in-car apps like Apple Music).

items.x:
Eiliko. | Photo by Sean Hollister / The Verge
There's a new digital pet in town - a cute little marshmallow of a robot that can change its cartoony expressions to match your mood. But if you or your kids talk to "Eiliko" over Wi-Fi, it'll phone home to China. Its AI companion can store literally everything you tell it on Chinese servers, where hackers can easily gain access or even hijack its personality. And the company that made it, Energize Lab , doesn't seem to care.
I bought an Eiliko from Amazon on August 29th. During a 10-minute conversation on August 30th, I asked the little bot: "Do you ever tell anybody else what I'm saying?"
"Your secrets are safe with me," it replied.

Google on Thursday said “Universal Cart,” a tool that lets users collect and monitor products they find across search and in the Gemini app, is now available to U.S. users. The company first previewed the tool at Google I/O in May.
The idea is to make online shopping easier to manage. Find something you like, save it to your cart, and move on. When you return later, your items and shopping progress are still there, so you don’t have to hunt down the same products or start over. Universal Cart can collect items from multiple retailers, turning it into a central hub for browsing and keeping track of potential purchases.
Google says the cart can also help shoppers stay on top of deals and availability. The tool can send notifications when a saved product’s price drops or when an out-of-stock item becomes available again.
The tool is also designed to offer more tailored help during the shopping process. Google says it can take credit card perks into account when helping users choose how to pay, and also surface relevant promo codes.
Checkout is tied to Google’s Universal Commerce Protocol, or UCP, an open standard the company introduced earlier this year.

items.t: StepFun Releases Open Weights for Step 5 Preview, Publishes Technical Blog on Its Architecture
items.d: Open weights for StepFun's Step 5 Preview are live: 600B total, 27B active, 1M context. A new technical blog explains its 92-layer design, Sparse GQA and long-horizon agent training.
items.x:
StepFun released the weights of its Step 5 Preview model on October 15, keeping the open-sourcing date it announced when the model launched in September. The release includes BF16 and FP8 checkpoints on Hugging Face and ModelScope, a technical blog describing how the model was built, and supporting open-source developer tools.
Step 5 Preview is a sparse mixture-of-experts model designed for long-horizon agent tasks. It has 600B total parameters, of which 27B are active per token, and supports a context window of up to 1 million tokens. StepFun says it performs well in coding, software engineering, professional knowledge work and finance. The company also says the model currently ranks second worldwide on OpenRouter's weekly and daily usage charts.
Developers can serve the model through an OpenAI-compatible API with vLLM or SGLang, or run offline inference with Transformers. According to the model card, the FP8 checkpoint fits on a single node of four B300 GPUs or eight H200 GPUs, while the BF16 checkpoint needs eight B300 GPUs or two eight-GPU H200 nodes. StepFun notes that the full BF16 sharded workflow for Transformers has not yet been validated end to end.
The weights are not under a standard open-source license.

items.t: Mathematicians Use Shanghai AI Lab's Intern-S2 to Prove 3D Ghys Conjecture, Verified in Lean
items.d: A proof of the codimension-one case of a 1995 conjecture by Etienne Ghys was developed with Intern-S2 over many rounds of dialogue, and a Peking University team formalized it in Lean.
items.x:
Shanghai AI Laboratory says its scientific multimodal model Intern-S2 helped mathematicians prove the three-dimensional case of the Ghys conjecture, a problem in complex dynamics posed in 1995 by the French mathematician Etienne Ghys. A team at Peking University then checked the main results with the Lean theorem prover.
The paper, Codimension-one holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphisms, was posted to arXiv on September 29 and revised on October 13. It lists a single author, Jiesong Zhang of KTH Royal Institute of Technology. It proves that every codimension-one holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphism of a compact connected complex manifold is biholomorphically conjugate to a hyperbolic automorphism of a complex torus, which settles the conjecture in that case and in complex dimension three. Roughly, the conjecture says that if a space supports this kind of chaotic but perfectly regular motion, the space itself must have a rigid, crystal-like structure.
The lab's announcement credits the work to a team led by Disheng Xu, a professor at Great Bay University and visiting scholar at the lab, with Zhang, his former student, joining as a visiting scholar.

items.t: Skywork Open-Sources Matrix-Game 4.0, Pairing a Game Engine With a Real-Time Video Model
items.d: Kunlun Tech's Skywork AI released Matrix-Game 4.0 under Apache-2.0: an engine runs the rules and physics while a causal video model renders low-poly frames into detailed game visuals.
items.x:
Skywork AI, the AI unit of Kunlun Tech, released Matrix-Game 4.0 on October 15, the latest version of its open-source interactive world model series. Inference code, a browser demo and the source code of three playable games are on GitHub, with model weights and game assets on Hugging Face. The new version is licensed under Apache-2.0.
The release changes how the series approaches game worlds. Instead of asking a video model to remember the world and keep track of the rules while it generates frames, Matrix-Game 4.0 keeps gameplay, physics and player input inside an executable game engine. The engine outputs a rough low-poly view of the scene, and a causal, few-step video model turns that view into detailed visuals in a streaming fashion. The team describes the approach as putting a harness on the video model: code decides what happens, and the model decides what it looks like.
That split means state such as health, item ownership and mission progress is recorded explicitly in code, so an occasional visual glitch does not rewrite the game. In a demo reported by QbitAI, a picked-up shield absorbs damage before the player's health drops, and the game ends when health reaches zero.

items.t: An update on independent evaluators

Last month, we committed to stronger independent, third-party assessment of our models and safety practices. We also signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, in which companies pledged to partner with independent external auditors or evaluators. Today, we’re announcing that we’ve started to give employee-like access to a team from METR, a nonprofit that evaluates frontier AI models.
METR will publish the results of its risk assessments. Over the past year, we’ve worked with METR on several reviews of our Risk Reports. We’re also working with SecureBio and Accenture as evaluators, and are in early discussions with several other organizations, including Hugging Face.
As models have become more powerful, they’ve required stronger safeguards and more challenging risk assessments. We want to be publicly accountable for the decisions we’re making. But we can’t publicly share all the information relevant to our safety work. Some of it could be useful to malicious actors, or is commercially sensitive, like compute or training information.

items.t: Apate sends AI agents undercover to get scammed so they can gather fraud intelligence

Most companies use AI agents to ship products faster or speed up workflows. Apate.ai sends them undercover to get scammed.
Founded in 2024 on the basis of research done in Macquarie University in Sydney, the Australian startup deploys thousands of AI agents that masquerade as innocent victims. The agents can answer scam calls, respond to shady messages and emails, follow phishing links, and join social media groups to bait fraudsters. They pretend to be people of all stripes, sporting different ages, genders and accents, and speak various languages as they try to keep scammers engaged long enough to learn something useful.
The company says its fleet of agents has so far wasted 17 years of scammers’ time across 2.5 million conversations. More importantly for Apate’s customer base of banks, telecom companies, government agencies and utilities, the undercover agents try to get scammers to reveal things about themselves that are usually learned only after a victim has been scammed: bank accounts, crypto wallets, phone numbers, malicious websites, the brands they’re impersonating, and other details about the scams they’re running.

items.t: Researchers use AI to design proteins that cut up other proteins
items.d: AI design tools make proteins that break bonds that are stable for hundreds of years.
items.x:
A protein is a chain of amino acids held together by what are called peptide bonds. On their own, those bonds are extremely stable; they're estimated to have a half-life of several hundred years. But in Earth's environment, most proteins don't last nearly that long. That's because organisms have evolved a handful of ways to catalyze the break-up of peptide bonds, which have diversified into countless specialized protein-digesting enzymes. Proteases are everywhere, and generally make short work of any proteins that find their way into the environment.
Now, researchers have basically short-circuited the diversification process, using AI-based protein design tools to take the catalytic core of two types of protease and replace the entire rest of the protein. The resulting enzymes could be tuned to cut specific proteins in half, and the researchers demonstrated their effectiveness by using them to cut proteins associated with neurological diseases.
The basic peptide bond isn't especially interesting-looking—it's what you get when you link an amino group to an acid, releasing a water molecule in the process. As their name implies, amino acids have both an amino and an acid group, allowing them to form peptide bonds on two sides of the amino acid.

items.t: My AI doppelganger tells me what to eat
items.d: This is Optimizer, a weekly newsletter sent from Verge senior reviewer Victoria Song that dissects and discusses the latest gizmos and potions that swear they're going to change your life. Opt in for Optimizer here. For the past 100 days…
items.x:
This week’s Optimizer delves into the concept of digital twins, a virtual version of a patient that can potentially help clinicians model medical treatments.
In return for feeding a ‘digital twin’ my metabolic data, it predicts how I’ll react to certain foods — and one day, maybe medicines.
For the past 100 days or so, my mornings have had a new rhythm. When I wake up, the first thing I have to do is feed my digital twin. It consumes my metabolic data, and its first “meal” of the day is my body composition data, sent straight from a smart scale.Once that’s logged in the app, I scoot over to the kitchen to fill an Owala with lemon water to take my medications with. That, too, gets logged in the app. On Mondays, I’ll follow that up with several calming breaths, measure my blood pressure, and offer that to the digital twin as well. Then it’s time to consider breakfast. I consult my digital twin.
My digital twin isn’t so much a robotic clone as it is an AI-powered, color-coded food database that predicts how my glucose levels will react to everything I eat. Red is not so good. Orange is so-so. Green is ideal. It’s built based on the data I feed it, as well as data collected from a continuous glucose monitor.
A bowl of protein Cheerios and milk?

items.t: Recording device hidden in toilet paper found in top-secret OpenAI meeting room
items.d: OpenAI engineer faces 5 years and $250K fine as FBI lobs foreign spy charges.
items.x:
It took OpenAI two days to notice that a recording device was hidden in a restricted executive conference room where leadership met to discuss highly confidential information, including technical progress, government engagements, and commercial partnerships.
Only those with special clearance are supposed to access that room. But the FBI believes the recording device was planted by Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old engineer from Saudi Arabia, who became a permanent US legal resident in 2020. In a press release Tuesday announcing his arrest, the FBI alleged that chatbot logs and CCTV footage suggested that Alfozan—who worked as an OpenAI engineer for more than a year—sought to use the device to spy on OpenAI and risked leaking trade secrets in a way that threatened national security.
To conceal the USB device, Alfozan allegedly wrapped it in toilet paper, then plugged it into the back of a conference room television. The device was likely planted on September 28, and OpenAI found it on September 30 and quickly determined that its contents were encrypted, the FBI said. Days later, on October 5, OpenAI installed a camera in that conference room, and the CCTV footage allegedly showed Alfozan attempting to retrieve the recording device that same day.

items.t: HiRO-ACEv2: Simulating extreme weather at 3 km resolution for a fraction of the cost
items.x:
Visualizing and using HiRO outputs 🤗 Models | 📄 Paper | 📓 Tutorial notebooks | 🌎 Demo
We introduce HiRO-ACEv2, the newest update to our High Resolution Output Ai2 Climate Emulator (HiRO-ACE) system. HiROv2 can reproduce even extremely rare rain, wind, and pressure events with high accuracy, while the full system can generate global 3 km climate data at about 1/300th the cost of X-SHiELD, a high-resolution global atmospheric model that explicitly simulates storms and other small-scale weather.
HiRO-ACE, introduced earlier in 2026, has two parts: ACE, an AI model that operates at a coarser 100 km resolution, and HiRO, a model that sharpens those coarse outputs into fine 3 km detail. The biggest change in HiRO-ACEv2 is the new downscaling model, HiROv2, which can now 1) predict several high-resolution fields at once instead of just rainfall, so it can capture a much wider range of extreme weather, and 2) has improved skill in predicting extreme events.
Our main focus with HiRO-ACEv2 was to simulate extreme events well. Changes to how we train HiROv2 improved its ability to reproduce the most intense rain, wind, and pressure values.

items.t: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
items.d: "Small weight-based replicators" could usher in a new generation of computer worms.
items.x:
AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet-of-things devices and is more resistant to takedown.
By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered. Still, the results do raise concerns about the possibility of new forms of computer worms.
Anthropic further warned not only about the new potential malware, but also that it could be difficult to stop. In its blog post, it wrote that “a replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off—though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days). Unlike non-AI malware, it could also figure out unfamiliar devices on its own.”

Amp chooses and recommends models based on what works best for its users, and OpenAI models account for the majority of tokens used in Amp. Quinn shares, “OpenAI is very transparent, and when there are safeguards applied, users know and they understand. That makes it really easy to use OpenAI models. As builders give agents more work, token costs can become a constraint. Quinn describes some Amp users consuming 10 billion tokens a week. He believes that if people watch every increment of usage, it might hold them back from finding out what an agent is capable of.

items.t: SentinelOne cuts malware analysis from weeks to hours
items.d: With OpenAI Daybreak, SentinelOne cuts weeks of malware analysis to hours, creating capacity to investigate more threats.
items.x:
With OpenAI Daybreak, SentinelOne cuts weeks of malware analysis to hours, creating capacity to investigate more threats.
Reverse engineering a sophisticated piece of malware can take a top security researcher four to six weeks. It’s painstaking work where researchers pull apart software to understand how it behaves, often retracing their steps as they uncover new information. Gregor Stewart, Chief AI Officer at SentinelOne, says OpenAI Daybreak can now produce human-level reverse-engineering output in roughly eight hours.
By reducing the time needed for deep analysis, OpenAI gives SentinelOne’s researchers room to investigate more malware and connect findings across samples. That wider view often reveals relationships that isolated investigations might miss. Stewart describes the opportunity as “a kind of intelligence that we were never able to afford before.”
Daybreak gives defenders access to OpenAI models for cybersecurity work. SentinelOne uses these capabilities to reverse engineer malware, examining software to understand how it behaves. Faster analysis gives its researchers more capacity to investigate additional samples.
Stewart emphasizes that his team remains responsible for the outcome. “The only thing that can’t be automated is accountability,” he says.

items.x:
Safety researchers continue to warn that a large volume of AI-generated explicit content is spreading unchecked, while regulators do little to meaningfully stop it.
This non-consensual content is commonly shared in text and direct messages or stored in private clouds where it’s less likely to be detected or reported, a Google co-authored study of Internet users across the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom found this July. That’s why the “most critical intervention point” remains at the source: the harmful AI tools used to make the fake sexual images, Google researchers concluded.
Yet red-teaming in recent months suggests that as some of the leading AI image generators from Google and OpenAI become more capable, they may be getting worse at blocking explicit outputs.

items.t: Dobot Launches VEGA 7, a Seven-Axis Force-Controlled Arm for Embodied AI With 50,000-Hour MTBF
items.d: Dobot's VEGA 7 has torque sensors and brakes in every joint, 0.15N force control accuracy, a 7kg payload and 725mm reach, aimed at wheeled dual-arm robots and embodied AI work.
items.x:
Dobot has launched DOBOT VEGA 7, a seven-axis force-controlled robotic arm designed from the start for embodied AI. The company unveiled it at a product event at the China International Industry Fair in Shanghai, positioning it for wheeled dual-arm robots, mobile manipulation in industrial settings and embodied AI development.
Dobot's main pitch is durability. The company says VEGA 7 has a mean time between failures of 50,000 hours. Every joint has an electromagnetic brake as standard, and in an unexpected power loss the arm can hold its posture and brake within 18 milliseconds. It is rated IP54 for dust and water resistance.
Every joint also carries a torque sensor, which supports contact sensing, compliant control, collision detection and hand-guided teaching. Dobot lists force control accuracy of 0.15N or better, torque control accuracy of 0.05N·m or better and force control resolution of 0.01N·m or better. The company says this makes the arm a development and validation platform for precise plugging and unplugging, small-part assembly and dual-arm coordination.

items.t: PHANES AI Launches SeePhys Hub, a Wearable Kit That Records Vision, Touch and Full-Body Motion
items.d: PHANES AI's SeePhys Hub pairs a four-camera headband with wrist, waist and leg trackers and tactile gloves, capturing human motion and touch data for training robots.
items.x:
PHANES AI has released SeePhys Hub, a whole-body, multimodal data capture system meant to turn everyday human activity into training data for robots. QbitAI reported that the October 14 launch was a joint release with Tinno Mobile, which contributed experience in cost control, supply chain and quality assurance, while PHANES AI focused on product design and algorithms.
The kit consists of a four-camera headband, two wrist bands, three motion trackers worn on the waist and lower legs, and a pair of tactile gloves. Together they record first-person vision with 360-degree coverage, hand pose and high-density touch, and whole-body pose and force.
The company's argument is that egocentric, or Ego, data from head-mounted cameras has become a key source for robot learning because it scales easily, but it misses much of what the body is doing. A camera at eye level sees the hands, yet often not the elbows or legs, and it records nothing about how hard the hands press on an object. Tasks that require walking, bending and two-handed coordination need that missing information.
SeePhys Hub uses a sparse-node approach. The three trackers combine IMU motion signals with UWB ranging between nodes, and algorithms fuse them with head and wrist vision to estimate full-body pose.

items.t: Doubao Phone Assistant Opens Screen Automation to Third-Party Apps as 151 Apps Opt Out

ByteDance's Doubao phone assistant said on October 14 that the 30-day public notice period for its Screen Automation Execution Protocol, or SAEP, has ended, and that it will now gradually open screen automation for third-party apps. Under the rules, apps whose developers have not declared a refusal will become available for the assistant's AI agent to operate on users' behalf.
The opt-out does not close with the notice period. Developers can still submit a refusal at any time, and the assistant said it will promptly switch off the related operations once it receives one. Apps that have already declared a refusal will not be operated by the agent.
Alongside the announcement, the assistant published its current list of apps that have refused and said the list will be updated regularly. According to a count by National Business Daily, it covers 151 apps, including 65 apps in the Tencent ecosystem such as WeChat, QQ and Honor of Kings, and 23 apps in the Alibaba ecosystem such as Taobao, Qwen and Alipay.
