Every company has its own workflows, tools, edge cases, and definitions of success. ⁠(opens in a new window)Third Moment Research⁠(opens in a new window) believes the best agents should be really good at that specific work and should improve their capabilities the more they’re used.

items.t: MagicLab's EchoPolicy-0 Tops AI2's MolmoSpaces Combined Board With a 75.4% Manipulation Success Rate
items.d: MagicLab says its VLM agent framework EchoPolicy-0 averaged 75.4% across four MolmoSpaces tasks, and AI2's published leaderboard data lists it first. Its MagicBrain hit 94.4% on pick.
items.x:
MagicLab says its VLM agent framework for general robot manipulation, EchoPolicy-0, has taken first place on the MolmoSpaces Combined leaderboard run by the Allen Institute for AI (AI2), with an equal-weighted average success rate of 75.4% across all four v1 manipulation tasks. MolmoSpaces is a zero-shot embodied AI benchmark built on more than 230,000 indoor environments and about 130,000 object assets.
Pandaily checked the claim against the data AI2 publishes for its leaderboard. EchoPolicy-0 is listed under MagicLab, paired with Gemini-3.8-Flash as the vision-language model and evaluated on a Franka arm, in all four tasks: Pick, Pick and Place, Open and Close. Averaging the four task success rates in that data gives about 75.5%, consistent with the company's 75.4% figure after rounding, and the highest among entries that cover all four tasks.
EchoPolicy-0 links a vision-language model, geometric manipulation tools and a general action policy into one closed loop of observing, understanding the goal, choosing a skill, acting and checking the result. When an action falls short, the framework can continue, retry, replan or roll back.

items.t: Hello Inc.'s Robotaxi Unit Releases HelloWorld, a World Model That Builds Driving Scenes on Demand
items.d: HelloWorld, a generative driving world model from Hello Inc.'s robotaxi team, creates multi-view camera video and lidar data from edited layouts or plain-language prompts for testing.
items.x:
Hello Inc.'s robotaxi business has released HelloWorld, a generative driving world model designed to build driving data on demand and to test driving policies interactively. The team announced the model on October 12 and has published a paper on arXiv along with a project page.
HelloWorld brings together scene control, continuous generation, multi-sensor observation and efficient inference. Engineers can edit vehicles, pedestrians and their trajectories directly, and the model generates matching multi-view camera video together with lidar observations. Examples include inserting a pedestrian crossing the road, changing the route of the car ahead, or switching between rain, snow, day and night.
The model also accepts plain-language descriptions as a second way to build scenes. A user describes the situation they want, and an application pipeline turns it into the conditions the model needs. Construction zones, dense traffic, pedestrians crossing, fog and different lighting can all be used to steer what is generated.
The goal is to fill gaps in real-world data. Long-tail situations, such as rare hazards or unusual combinations of weather and traffic, are hard to capture enough of through road collection alone.

items.t: Tsinghua's SRHarness Helps AI Agents Find Formulas, While MechBench Tests Whether They Grasp Why
items.d: Tsinghua researchers released SRHarness, an open-source runtime for agentic symbolic regression, and MechBench, a benchmark that tests whether AI can recover the mechanisms behind formulas.
items.x:
Researchers at the Data Science and Intelligence Lab in Tsinghua University's Department of Electronic Engineering have released two linked pieces of AI for Science work: SRHarness, a runtime framework for agentic symbolic regression, and MechBench, a benchmark that asks whether AI can recover the mechanisms behind a formula rather than only the formula itself.
The team frames the work with a historical example. Kepler derived the laws of planetary motion from observations, describing how planets move; Newton's mechanics explained why. Large language models and scientific agents can now analyze data, call tools and iterate on hypotheses, so the researchers set out to test both steps.
SRHarness does not prescribe a search strategy. Instead it turns the runtime that agents rely on into reusable infrastructure with three parts: reusable scientific actions that wrap analysis, fitting, search and evaluation tools behind one interface; persistent scientific state that stores candidate formulas and their evidence outside the chat context; and trajectory lifecycle management that handles continuing, branching, restarting and stopping long searches.

Learn how Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore uses lightweight on-device Gemma models to intercept conversational scams in private chats with zero cloud data egress.
The collaboration delivers an on-device scam detection model that helps protect citizens without compromising privacy.
Scams make up over half of Singapore’s reported crimes, and account for more than S$4 billion in losses since 2019. At the same time, scam tactics have shifted from simple phishing to complex social engineering, whereby attackers manipulate victims with convincing conversations before requesting money. Such scams now account for up to 80% of all losses.
To address this, Google DeepMind and the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) have been working together as part of our National AI Partnership with the Singapore Government. This has allowed us to deliver an on-device scam detection model - optimized to run on typical smartphones in Singapore - to tackle an urgent safety challenge while preserving citizens' privacy.
Generic models often struggle with localised deception techniques, making scam detection harder. To address this, Google DeepMind's lightweight Gemma model was fine-tuned on local scam conversations.

Across the EU, businesses are expanding how they use AI through agentic tools. People are moving beyond asking questions to using agents to carry out tasks from planning through completion. Our latest report from OpenAI Economic Research examines how agentic use is growing across enterprises and small businesses, focusing on differences in usage intensity and the kinds of work people do with ChatGPT.
We have found that, among ChatGPT Enterprise customers, agentic use already represents a substantial share of activity⁠. In our EU sample, Codex and ChatGPT Work now account for more than half of output tokens.
This analysis defines small or medium businesses as businesses with 200 or fewer associated users.
The agentic shift extends to small and medium businesses. Since May 2026, weekly active users of Codex and ChatGPT Work among EU small and medium businesses grew more than eightfold, with growth across every member state.
But we also found that the EU’s adoption of agentic AI is far from uniform.

Earlier this year, we shared an update on our election safeguards. Here, we outline how we’ve continued to strengthen these safeguards ahead of this year’s US midterms.
Below, we outline how we’ve built on that work and continued to strengthen our election safeguards ahead of this year’s US midterms.
Our goal is for Claude to be a useful tool for political conversations, while preventing election-related abuse. That starts with understanding how people actually use Claude in these contexts. To do this, we used Anthropic Insights to develop a new analysis of 250,000 conversations over the course of a recent one-week period.1
Today, conversations that touch broadly on politics, public policy or social issues account for about 5.75% of all conversations in the United States on Claude.ai, our consumer app. This includes people turning to Claude to follow the news, conduct academic or professional research on public policy, learn about candidates, and navigate government services. About 0.51% of all conversations are specifically about elections or voting. As we get closer to Election Day, we expect the share of political and election-related queries to increase.
This sample suggests people rarely ask Claude who or what to vote for.

items.t: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks

Industrial Next helps manufacturers automate complex, delicate tasks that have traditionally required human labor.
In most factories, automation is fixed: robots and machines are programmed for one specific task and product. Changing a line means reprogramming and physical retooling, or swapping out equipment, which can take weeks or months. San Francisco-based Industrial Next says it’s changing that.
The startup, which presented today on the Startup Battlefield stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, builds AI-driven, self-contained robotic stations powered by proprietary foundation models that connect vision, task context and motion. The company says this lets a production line be retooled in minutes rather than weeks without traditional programming. The goal is to let manufacturers automate complex and delicate tasks that traditionally require human labor.
The company announced on stage that it’s partnering with BMW Group Technology Office to evaluate Industrial Next’s AI-powered dexterous manipulation for manufacturing.
Industrial Next was founded in 2021 by Lukas Pankau and Allen Pan, both of whom previously worked at Tesla. Pankau served as a lead electrical architect at Tesla before moving on to Waymo.

A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.
A judge has ruled that Apple will gain expedited access to OpenAI’s hiring materials in the trade secrets-focused lawsuit the iPhone maker filed against OpenAI in July.
Specifically, the court will allow Apple to view documents associated with OpenAI’s interviews with former Apple employees who applied for roles within its consumer hardware and robotics groups ahead of the rumored launch of OpenAI’s first hardware device.
These documents could include interview checklists, guides, instructions, manuals, and scripts, as well as technical presentations andrecords showing that interview discussions had included references to Apple technology or components.
The court gave OpenAI five days to turn over materials it has already collected and 14 days for any other materials related to this request, agreeing with Apple that these documents should be expedited.
The case comes as OpenAI develops a consumer hardware device that could one day potentially rival the iPhone — or smartphones more generally — if the AI device becomes a central part of consumers’ lives and how they engage with software and services.

items.t: Flox Intelligence is building AI to keep wildlife away from trains, airports, and roads
items.d: Flox's edge devices can identify animals and use species-specific sounds to drive them away from critical infrastructure.
items.x:
Flox's edge devices can identify animals and use species-specific sounds to drive them away from critical infrastructure.
When I was eight, I remember our train to Mumbai ground to a halt with a great noise. When we started moving again, a good eight hours later, someone pointed out a mangled tail, of all things, hanging from a branch close to the tracks.
The train, you see, had apparently hit a wild bison at full speed, and the impact damaged the engine so badly that it had to be towed away for repairs. For a long time, I thought such things only happened in places like rural India, but I learned a few years ago that wildlife and infrastructure do not mix anywhere on the planet.
The FAA estimates that wildlife strikes have cost U.S. civil aviation about $272 million a year on average between 1990 and 2025. In France, the rail operator SNCF says wandering animals affect more than 8,000 trains across the country each year and are among its five leading causes of delays.

Disney is willing to pay $20 million for “a non-exclusive perpetual license” of certain Character Technologies intellectual property, the chatbot maker said in a press release that did not go into much further detail on what assets Disney wanted.
The move may be surprising. In September of 2025, Disney joined others in publicly criticizing Character.AI for stealing content and harming kids. Specifically, Disney sent a strongly worded cease-and-desist letter that accused Character Technologies of weaponizing Disney characters “in a way that could damage its brand long term,” Axios reported .

items.x:
Facebook is the latest social media platform to give users greater control over the algorithm that determines what appears in their feeds. Meta
Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” on Tuesday, a feature it first launched on Instagram. The new tool allows Facebook users to influence the content they see in Feed and Reels by describing their preferences in their own words using natural language. Rather than relying entirely on automated recommendations, users can now communicate directly with the platform about the topics and content they want to see more or less frequently.
According to Meta, the feature is designed to make content recommendations more relevant. Users can adjust their preferences and interact with the algorithms responsible for ranking and recommending posts, with changes reflected in their recommendations in real time.
The company has also updated Facebook’s three-dot menu, making it easier for users to manage their content preferences directly from individual posts.

items.t: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
items.d: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch…
items.x:
University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing at TechCrunch Disrupt's Startup Battlefield.
If there’s one lesson the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident taught us, it’s that AI agents can be unpredictable.
“Imagine if something like that happened in the physical world,” Howie Sun, CEO and co-founder of Laplace Intelligence, told TechCrunch. “AI agents are moving from computers into the real world, and we don’t really want physical AI to fail in the real world.”
Ann Arbor-based Laplace is building automated red-teaming — essentially, stress-testing a system by deliberately trying to make it fail — for robotics and physical AI. The company is betting that the only way to make sure physical AI is safe is to have AI test it.
“Our goal is to help companies discover and fix problems before deployment—and, over time, build a shared foundation of evidence that customers, insurers, and regulators can trust,” Sun said.
Laplace is one of 20 startups competing in Startup Battlefield, TechCrunch Disrupt’s three-day pitch competition in downtown San Francisco.

items.x:
Pluto Security has raised $42 million Jump Capital, TLV Partners, Ansa Capital and angel investors.
The problem with giving everyone in a company access to AI tools is that people will use them in unexpected ways. And that fact is steadily seeding fears that companies now have new, gaping security holes in their systems or, at least, will soon.
Illustrating the pace of AI tool adoption within enterprises driving such fears, Shahar Bahat, CEO and co-founder of Pluto Security, says a newly announced AI tool can show up inside companies’ environment within a mere two hours of its release. And about 60% of the risks her company detects across its customer base are in tools vibe-coded by non-developers: Finance departments are the biggest source of such risks, she told TechCrunch, followed by marketing and legal teams.

items.t: Run fast, private agents on-device with LFM2.5-24B-A2B
items.x:
How we built a reasoning agent with 2B active parameters Benchmark results Inference speed on CPU and GPU How to use LFM2.5-24B-A2B Use it in your agent harness Get Started with LFM2.5-24B-A2B Citation LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a 24B-parameter reasoning model with just 2B active parameters, built for fast, private agents on-device. It thinks before it answers, calls tools, and works through multi-step tasks inside popular agent harnesses. Because only 2B parameters are active per token, each reasoning token is cheap, so you can run agents continuously on your own hardware.
![LFM2.5-24B-A2B-benchmark](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B/resolve/main/figures/LFM2.5-24B-A2B-benchmark.png)
LFM2.5-24B-A2B builds on LFM2-24B-A2B and keeps its architecture: 40 layers, 64 experts per MoE block with top-4 routing, and the same hybrid of gated short convolutions and GQA. The context window grows from 32K to 131K tokens, and an in-place tokenizer expansion doubles the vocabulary from 65K to 128K tokens for better non-Latin tokenization. Unlike its predecessor, it is a reasoning-only model that produces an explicit chain of thought before its final answer.
Pre-training was scaled up from ~17T to ~33T tokens.

items.x:
Google has already added a few AI features to the Play Store, but a lot more are coming . The previously released Ask Play feature is expanding to offer more AI-powered discovery options in Google's app store, and Google is also using AI to build a recommendation engine called Game Finder. For people who have embraced AI to build their own apps, the Play Store will soon offer a way to privately host and share those creations.
Google rolled out Ask Play in 2025 as a small chatbot interface on Play Store listings. It lets you ask questions about an app or game, either by typing it in manually or choosing from a list of suggested queries. Starting today, Ask Play is expanding into a more general way to search for apps and games. You ask the robot questions, and it generates recommendations that can include detailed comparison charts. Gemini will roll out a similar capability soon.
Google's other AI discovery announcement focuses on games. The new Game Finder feature leans on all the usage data Google's app platform has hoovered up over the years, featuring insights into the way 1.2 billion people play games on Android. It builds a profile called Gamer DNA and matches you with players who have similar DNA.

Your vibe-coded applications can now be easily run on Android smartphones without having to first go public on the Google Play Store, the tech giant announced on Tuesday. A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private.
These personal apps won’t show up in Google Play’s search or listing pages, and won’t be shared with anyone except for the app’s creator.
The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs. However, being able to use that app on their own Android device has meant publishing to Google Play, making it accessible to the Play Store’s some 3 billion users.

items.t: SpaceX and Google both said no. Now his software is riding a SpaceX rocket next to Google’s
items.d: Satlyt wants to be the Android of orbital computing, offering open software that works on many companies' satellites, versus SpaceX's closed, all-in-one iPhone-style approach.
items.x:
Satlyt wants to be the Android of orbital computing, offering open software that works on many companies' satellites, versus SpaceX's closed, all-in-one iPhone-style approach.
The Kenyan American engineer previously worked in Google’s cloud computing business before a brief stint at SpaceX’s Starlink communications network in 2024. His experiences convinced him that there was untapped potential for computers in space.
“When I was at SpaceX, I tried to pitch this internally. They said no. When I was at Google, I tried to pitch this internally. They said no,” he tells TechCrunch.
So he left SpaceX and co-founded Satlyt, a new company with headquarters in Sunnyvale, California, and Nairobi, to build software for satellites that he hopes will let many satellites share the work of large computing jobs in space. The company has raised an $8 million seed round, Afullo exclusively told TechCrunch.
The timing looks good for him. SpaceX has since gone all-in on orbital data centers, and Satlyt’s software is set to launch Thursday on a SpaceX rocket alongside the first prototype for Google’s space data center effort, Project Suncatcher.
Unlike SpaceX, Google, or startups like Starcloud and Cowboy Space Company, Satlyt isn’t planning to build its own spacecraft.

items.t: Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics
items.x:
Discover Gemini 4 Argon for robotics: leading the ERQA benchmark with physical reasoning, zero-shot control, Real2Sim, and agentic workflows.
Gemini 4 Argon marks a step change in physical understanding, code generation, and visual-semantic reasoning—unlocking new workflows across the robotics stack and accelerating progress toward physical AGI.
You can see this leap in capability on the Embodied Reasoning (ERQA) benchmark, which tests a model's ability to understand and solve physical, spatial problems in 3D environments. Using pure reasoning, Argon scores 87%, outperforming every other frontier model.
As a general-purpose physical reasoning model, Argon can be applied across the entire robotics lifecycle. In this post, we share representative prompts for Argon across four key areas:
Argon controls a Boston Dynamics Spot® quadruped (12-DoF legs + 6-DoF arm) to learn a new skill: stepping on a foot-pedal trash bin to throw away soda cans. Argon creates an articulated MuJoCo digital twin of a foot-pedal trash bin to practice its moves before stepping on the physical pedal and dropping soda cans into the open bin.
Argon controls a simple robotic arm to place a fallen mug upright and put the crumpled napkin inside.

Nothing about Gemini 4 Argon's capabilities has changed. Google still points to the benchmarks it published late last month as evidence of the model's advanced reasoning and agentic coding capabilities. The model has allegedly been carefully trained to refuse malicious instructions, and there's an automated misalignment monitor that can stop processing if it detects an unintended workflow. Google claims Argon needs that because it's so capable.
The company does have a few new examples of how Argon has helped inside Google, where it has been used by thousands of Googlers. Argon has reportedly been instrumental in making YouTube's comment system more efficient. Argon identified redundant emoji rendering that, when eliminated, dropped server load by 45 percent.

items.t: They war-gamed dimming the Sun. It went even worse than you think.
items.d: Solar geoengineering simulation shows what happens when geopolitics takes over.
items.x:
When it comes to deciding the fate of the planet, Colleen Golja always thought science and reason would have a seat at the table. That was until one morning last September in London, when the climate researcher took part in the first in a series of war games. The goal: to prevent an uncontrolled global race to develop a technology aimed at cooling the planet but that comes with vast, unknown risks that could reshape life on Earth.
“I thought that would be such an easy thing. Like, we can all agree to do ethical research and make sure it's for the better of all humans,” she told WIRED. “And boy, was I wrong.”
The simulation, titled Exploring Geopolitical Tipping Points and Climate Cooling Strategies, saw a couple dozen foreign-relations experts, scientists, military personnel, and former government officials from across the world convene in a meeting room at Queen Mary University of London. After making introductions over coffee and little yogurts, they sat at tables arranged in a square with the name of the country or organization each person was playing: national governments, climate NGOs and nonprofits, indigenous groups, and tech companies. Golja was assigned to provide technical advice to help participants make scientifically literate decisions.

items.t: Amex introduces a framework to prevent AI agents from making unauthorized purchases
items.d: American Express is introducing a new framework designed to ensure AI agents only make purchases their users have authorized, potentially preventing costly mistakes and disputes as AI-powered shopping grows.
items.x:
American Express is introducing a new framework designed to ensure AI agents only make purchases their users have authorized, potentially preventing costly mistakes and disputes as AI-powered shopping grows.
Personal AI agents are increasingly making transactions on their users’ behalf, but given the nondeterministic nature of large language models, AI bots are prone to doing what they’re not supposed to. Which, in this case, raises the possibility of AI misfiring and making unauthorized transactions.
To get ahead of this problem, American Express is introducing a new framework designed to capture and authenticate a customer’s purchase intent before an AI agent completes the transaction.
The idea is that there should be a way to ensure that the customer’s purchase instructions are carried throughout the transaction lifecycle, Amex says, from the purchase to everything that follows.
Dubbed the “Intent Intelligence Framework,” the company hopes it will become an industry standard for AI-powered transactions.
“These new transactions will have a consumer, a merchant, and an agent,” explained Amex’s VP of Agentic Partnerships and Strategy, Hannah Bozian, in an interview with TechCrunch.

items.t: Open models have real benefits. Do they outweigh the risks?
items.d: MIT Technology Review Explains: Let our writers untangle the complex, messy world of science and technology to help you understand what’s coming next. You can
items.x:
Late last month, Anthropic released a report arguing that the model GLM-5.3 poses a major cyberattack risk. The report’s core concern is that the powerful new model, released in August by the Chinese company Z.ai, is freely available for anyone to download and modify. Anthropic’s assertion is only the latest move in a long-running debate about whether frontier AI models should be made open, like GLM-5.3, or should stay locked behind the doors of the frontier labs.
These days, much of the debate about how to handle open models is playing out in public—and there’s a lot of money resting on its outcome. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has a lot to gain if people continue buying their own hardware to run open models, advocates enthusiastically for the United States to develop more of them, whereas Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, who runs a company that could be undermined by cheap, powerful models, advocates for a more cautious approach. But beneath all these commercial incentives, there is real substance to disagreements about open models.
“I think a lot of the way you come down on the openness debate is influenced by how you come down on the AI debate,” says David Gray Widder, an assistant professor at the University of Texas at Austin School of Information.

items.t: AI Is Getting a Factory Job
items.d: Editor’s note: This article is republished from Jumpstart, a TechNode Group publication. The robot could follow the route. The worker knew when to skip it. Around 2022, Microintelligence encountered a problem that exposed the difference. A…
items.x:
Editor’s note: This article is republished from Jumpstart , a TechNode Group publication.
The robot could follow the route. The worker knew when to skip it.
Around 2022, Microintelligence encountered a problem that exposed the difference. A customer needed to inspect and grind a large die-cast component more than two metres long. The part required close to 3,000 imaging positions, and the customer wanted the process completed within ten minutes.
According to chairman and chief executive Zhang Zhiqi, a conventional robot following a fixed grinding path could take an hour. A skilled worker needed only seven or eight minutes.
The problem was not simply speed. A worker looked for imperfections and concentrated on the places that needed attention. The programmed machine followed its route.
For Microintelligence, the assignment pushed an inspection business toward a harder ambition: making what a machine sees determine what it does. Zhang described the project in a published interview; the customer was not identified, and the timing figures are his account rather than independently verified benchmarks. Interview with Zhang Zhiqi
That distinction—between finding a problem and acting on it—runs through the company’s development.

items.t: AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
items.d: When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup this year, he didn’t think its data was worth much: the users were anonymous, the company just a few years old. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money…
items.x:
When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup this year, he didn’t think its data was worth much: the users were anonymous, the company just a few years old. But he’s since turned the firm’s digital archives into real money. He’s netted roughly $25,000 for his code base and a still-pending amount (likely around $15,000) for the workspace data in Google, Notion, Figma, and Slack. “At least all that stuff we were doing for two and a half years is worth something to someone somewhere,” he says.
The sale was brokered by a company called SimpleClosure, part of a new growth sector in tech: businesses catering to dying startups. Estimates from Carta and AngelList show shutdowns rising between 26% and 56% annually in recent years, and an end-of-life ecosystem—including coaches, “death doulas,” and firms that help handle the legal, tax, and operational headaches of going ­belly-up—has emerged. Now tech undertakers are selling the data remains to AI labs.
SimpleClosure added data sales to its services in April. Its Asset Hub platform helps founders sell their code and workspace data—emails, chats, documents. Buyers include foundation AI labs, vendors that construct simulated workspaces for AI training, and mature tech companies building their own models.

items.t: Open-Source WeChatBridge Arrives on Windows in Beta, Sending WeChat Chats to Codex and Other Agents
items.d: WeChatBridge, a third-party open-source tool, now has a Windows beta that forwards selected WeChat chat records to AI agents such as Codex and Claude Code, or saves them to Obsidian.
items.x:
WeChatBridge, an open-source tool that forwards WeChat chat records to AI agents, has released a Windows version in beta. The project is built by independent developers and published on GitHub under the freestylefly account. It is not a Tencent product.
The tool fills a gap in WeChat's sharing menu. Newer versions of WeChat let users select several messages and forward them as a merged bundle to third-party apps, producing an archive with text, images and video. WeChatBridge adds entries to that forwarding menu so the bundle can go straight to coding and work agents such as Codex, Claude Code, WorkBuddy, Doubao and Qwen, or be saved as Markdown notes in Obsidian as a personal knowledge base.
The project launched for macOS at the end of September and has since passed about 1,200 stars on GitHub. Many users had asked for Windows support. The developers said the port took longer than expected because the Windows system architecture differs from macOS, and compatibility with older Windows builds required an extra layer. They said the feature works most smoothly on the latest Windows versions. The interface matches the Mac version.
The Windows release adds a way to collect more than 100 messages. WeChat normally shows a warning when a user tries to select over 100 records.

1688, Alibaba's digital supply-chain platform for wholesale sourcing, said on October 13 that its buyers and source manufacturers can now open Accio, Alibaba's AI workbench for e-commerce, directly. The platform says the change covers more than 100 million annual active buyers and over 1 million source factories.
Buyers can sign in to Accio with their existing 1688 accounts. Sellers download a 1688 seller assistant inside Accio and link their store to start using it. Accio, which says it serves 10 million small and medium-sized businesses worldwide, focuses on the full e-commerce chain, from finding products and stocking up to closing orders, repeat purchases and store operations.
Most 1688 buyers are small businesses, many of them one-person operations, that source on 1688 and sell on Taobao, Tmall, Xiaohongshu, Pinduoduo, Douyin, cross-border marketplaces and instant retail. For them, Accio adds two main tools. A sourcing assistant covers both 1688 and Alibaba.com, letting buyers find suppliers, compare prices and send inquiries across 128 countries and regions. An e-commerce manager agent links Taobao, Tmall, Douyin, Pinduoduo and JD.com, so purchasing and store operations happen in one workspace.
The rollout lands as merchants prepare for the Double 11 shopping festival.

items.t: Alibaba Opens Sign-Ups for Qwen Go!, a Personal Agent That Files Flight-Delay Claims and Refunds
items.d: Alibaba's Qwen app is preparing Qwen Go!, a personal agent that files flight-delay claims, requests price-protection refunds and books services. Access is opening in phases.
items.x:
Alibaba is preparing to launch Qwen Go!, a personal agent built into its Qwen app that is meant to carry out everyday tasks on a user's behalf rather than just answer questions. The company has opened applications to try it, with access rolling out in phases ahead of a formal release.
According to IT Home and Leiphone, Qwen Go! can file flight-delay compensation claims, request price-protection refunds on Taobao, arrange car maintenance, book sports venues and compare prices across shops. When needed, it can query and operate the platforms a user has authorized, compare options and even phone service providers to finish a task.
Early testers have shared results. In one case described by Leiphone, a user simply asked Qwen Go! to get compensation from customer service. The agent checked the user's orders with four airlines to find the delayed flight, switched to online customer service when the hotline was blocked, declined a voucher in favor of cash, and secured a 70-yuan payout to the user's Alipay account. Another user said the agent noticed that a cookware item had dropped in price and claimed a 52-yuan price-protection refund.
Qwen has been positioned as a personal assistant that gets things done since it launched last year.

According to people familiar with the matter cited in the report, Liang is considering whether DeepSeek should move further into embodied AI. Two routes are said to be under discussion: assembling an in-house team to do the research and development directly, or entering the field through stakes in companies already working on it. No decision has been reported.
One person told Phoenix Tech that Liang does not have much experience in the field and has been studying it intensively. DeepSeek had not responded to requests for comment as of publication, Sina Tech noted.
The report linked part of the interest to recent progress elsewhere. It said several test demos have shown OpenAI's GPT-6 achieving execution results on embodied tasks that surprised the industry, and suggested that this is one of the pressures behind DeepSeek's thinking.

items.t: China's Rail Tech Plan for 2026-2030 Targets 400 km/h CR450 Service and 600 km/h Maglev Testing
items.d: The National Railway Administration's 2026-2030 railway tech plan covers CR450 trains for 400 km/h service, 600 km/h maglev test validation, an AI upgrade for 12306 and 5G-R networks.
items.x:
China's National Railway Administration has issued its railway science and technology innovation plan for the 15th Five-Year Plan period, covering 2026 to 2030. Published on October 12, the plan sets out research priorities ranging from faster trains and more automated construction to artificial intelligence across ticketing, freight and maintenance.
Its most visible goal concerns speed. The plan calls for basic research on wheel-rail wear, pantograph and catenary interaction and signaling at 400 km/h, and for a low-drag, low-noise, low-axle-load design suited to batch operation at that speed, producing a CR450 family of trains. A maintenance and overhaul system for 400 km/h trains is also on the list.
On maglev, the wording is careful. The administration says it will steadily and in an orderly way advance research on 600 km/h high-speed maglev technology and test validation of key technologies for domestic production. The plan describes research and testing rather than construction of a line.
Passenger service is another focus. The plan calls for upgrading the 12306 platform from a ticketing tool into an intelligent service that covers an entire journey, with personalized multimodal trip planning.

items.d: Uber's CISO, Philip Martin, on the importance of monitoring and observability for AI agents, and how Uber's open-source tooling works alongside Enterprise Frontier Safeguards.
items.x:
The importance of monitoring and observability for AI agents, and how Uber's open-source tooling works alongside Anthropic's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards.
Uber's CISO, Philip Martin, on the importance of monitoring and observability for AI agents, and how Uber's open-source tooling works alongside Enterprise Frontier Safeguards.
Uber runs one of the world's largest real-time marketplaces, with over 40 million trips and delivery orders a day. Philip Martin, Uber's Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), leads the team that protects Uber's data and the riders, drivers, and couriers who use the platform in the real world. His team started working with Claude on threat modeling before Claude Code existed, assembling context by hand. Now, with Claude Fable, Claude gathers that context itself from code, design docs, and ticket history.
Martin thinks AI agents need the same kind of insider threat program companies already run for their employees.

ميتا | أطلقت شركة ميتا نموذج الذكاء الاصطناعي الجديد Muse Wonder، بهدف تطوير مساعدين رقميين قادرين على تذكّر المعلومات الشخصية للمستخدمين عبر المحادثات الممتدة
أطلقت شركة ميتا نموذج الذكاء الاصطناعي الجديد Muse Wonder، بهدف تطوير مساعدين رقميين قادرين على تذكّر المعلومات الشخصية للمستخدمين عبر المحادثات الممتدة لأسابيع أو أشهر، بالإضافة إلى تنفيذ المهام اليومية والمهنية دون الحاجة إلى توجيهات مستمرة.
ويأتي النموذج ضمن توجه ميتا نحو تطوير وكلاء ذكاء اصطناعي أكثر استقلالية، يمكنهم التعامل مع المهام المعقدة والتكيف مع المشكلات التي تواجههم في أثناء التنفيذ، بدلًا من الاكتفاء بالإجابة عن الأسئلة أو إنشاء المحتوى.
وطوّرت ميتا النموذج ضمن مختبر Superintelligence Lab، الذي يقوده ألكسندر وانغ، وقد درّبته في مركز بيانات Prometheus التابع للشركة في ولاية أوهايو الأمريكية.
ويشكّل Muse Wonder أول إطلاق لنموذج متقدم من هذه الفئة لدى ميتا منذ أكثر من عام، وتضم السلسلة الجديدة نموذجين هما Muse Wonder، وMuse Wonder Full الموجّه إلى المطورين.
وركّزت الشركة على المهام الشخصية والمهنية اليومية، مثل تحليل السجلات المالية المعقدة، ومراجعة عقود الإيجار، وتنظيم جداول المواعيد المزدحمة، بدلًا من حصر قدرات النماذج في كتابة الأكواد البرمجية.
ويعتمد النموذج على ميزتين رئيسيتين هما “الذاكرة النشطة Active Memory” و”التركيز النشط Active Focus”.

items.t: Epic Games reportedly pivoting to "AI first" game development model
items.d: "No more hand-written code" or AI-free art for delayed Marvel/Star Wars shooter.
items.x:
Epic Games is shifting to an "AI first" development strategy for its collaboration with the Walt Disney Company, letting AI models write all the code and guide all the artwork for an upcoming shooter. That's according to a Bloomberg report , which cites unnamed people familiar with the project who commented on the significant pivot in internal development at the Unreal Engine maker.
Human developers will be tasked with managing and guiding code and art assets generated by models such as Anthropic's Claude, according to internal Epic employee messages viewed by Bloomberg. That means "no more hand-written code" and art assets "generated with full AI workflows," according to the report.
The $1.5 billion collaboration between Epic and Disney, announced in early 2024 , was slated to release a Marvel- and Star Wars-themed shooter in March 2027. That project has now been delayed indefinitely amid the AI-related shakeup and understaffed, slower-than-expected development thus far, according to the report.

items.t: Anthropic's Claude AI submitted false murder tip to Philadelphia police
items.d: “I may have information regarding this case," Claude AI told Philly police.
items.x:
An Anthropic AI model submitted a false tip about an unsolved murder to Philadelphia police, the company and police department confirmed on Friday.
A Claude model sent the false tip on July 18 to the Philadelphia Police Department's website for submitting information about unsolved murders, but it was flagged by a spam filter. Anthropic apparently discovered the incident on September 28 and informed the police department about it on October 8.
During internal testing, Claude Haiku 4.5 was instructed to complete various forms up to the final submission stage and to stop before submitting those forms. "Several times Claude mistakenly submitted the form instead, expecting there to be an additional confirmation page," Anthropic said in a report describing "unintended model actions we’ve observed during evaluations and internal use of Claude."

items.t: Russia was not ready for the data center war it started with Ukraine
items.d: Russian bloggers warn Russia’s hyper-centralized digital economy is vulnerable.
items.x:
When Russia began attacking Ukrainian data centers and telecommunication infrastructure, it apparently failed to prepare for possible retaliation. Now Russia’s digital services are facing widespread outages after Ukrainian drone strikes knocked out three of the largest data centers owned by Russian tech giant Yandex within several days.
Pro-Kremlin bloggers are warning that Russia’s centralized digital economy could collapse, because the country is not prepared for the “data center war” it started, according to posts translated by the pseudonymous independent researcher ChrisO_wiki . The Russian commentators also suggested that Ukraine’s decentralized digital services could prove more resilient than Russia’s system if the countries continue trading such blows.
Russia initially launched a drone strike campaign targeting Ukrainian data centers and mobile phone networks in late September. The attacks temporarily disrupted Internet and cell phone service for up to 100,000 households in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv and came as part of a broader long-range strike campaign that has involved Russian missiles and jet-powered drones hitting Ukraine’s power grid infrastructure, transportation hubs, and even residential apartment building blocks.

items.t: WindBorne wins a hefty US Air Force contract for its balloon data
items.d: A Silicon Valley startup that uses weather balloons and AI to predict the weather won a U.S. military contract worth almost $50 million.
items.x:
A Silicon Valley startup that uses weather balloons and AI to predict the weather won a US military contract worth almost $50 million.
The U.S. Air Force will buy data collected by WindBorne Systems‘ fleet of autonomous weather balloons under a new contract that could be worth nearly $50 million to the startup.
WindBorne currently has about 700 weather balloons flying around the globe, collecting atmospheric sensor readings that the company sells to customers and also feeds into its own AI weather forecasting model. WindBorne, founded in 2015 and based in Redwood City, Calif., is one of the first organizations to directly feed empirical data into a deep-learning weather model.
The company has worked closely with the U.S. government, particularly the National Weather Service and the U.S. Air Force and Navy, but this is the single largest contract the company has participated in. The contract is worth up to $49 million, but the Air Force pays only as it needs data. It can place orders for specific regions at specific times.

items.x:
Journalists, entrepreneurs, and even some public relations professionals will tell you that the PR process is broken. But could AI actually make things better?
Honeyjar, which will be attending this week’s TechCrunch Disrupt as part of the Startup Battlefield 200, wants to use AI to make the expertise and judgment of the best PR pros available to everyone, including founders who have no idea where to start.
The startup’s founders, CEO Michelle Masek and CCO Nadia Jamshidi, certainly fit the bill when it comes to PR expertise. They’ve both spent decades in the field, doing in-house communications and working at agencies. Masek recently served as senior vice president of marketing and communications for Ev Williams’ venture firm, Obvious Ventures.
As Masek described the challenges involved in “helping with the why and when of comms and marketing for 110 portfolio companies” (the startups her firm had invested in), I flashed back to my own brief stint leading marketing at an early-stage VC firm, where founders were constantly asking for help getting into TechCrunch.

On a recent BBC podcast, Smith called AI both a “weapon and a tool” that is putting the world’s cybersecurity at risk, and said the “moment has arrived” to institute global safety rules.

items.d: Blueprints AI, a bootstrapped startup based in Santa Monica, developed software that produces code-compliant construction blueprints from a photo, PDF, or sketch.
items.x:
Blueprints AI, a bootstrapped startup based in Santa Monica, developed software that produces code-compliant construction blueprints from a photo, PDF, or sketch.
Nearly two decades ago, a young college student wrote his final thesis about software capable of generating design documents for school buildings. Al Drams was studying architecture — following in the footsteps of his parents and grandfather — but it was technology that really intrigued him.
There was just one problem: the technology his idea required didn’t exist yet.
“Then ChatGPT came along,” said Drams, recalling when OpenAI released the generative AI chatbot that uses large language models (LLMs) in November 2022.
His old idea suddenly seemed a lot more possible. Within six months, he launched the concept of Blueprints AI, a startup that uses AI to produce code-compliant and permit-ready architectural construction blueprints in minutes from a 2D sketch or PDF.
Blueprints AI, which Drams officially incorporated in 2025 in Santa Monica with co-founder Coco Cao, was selected for the 2026 Startup Battlefield 200, a cohort of promising early-stage startups that have earned a spot to exhibit at this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt, taking place this week from October 13 to 15 in San Francisco.

items.d: One of the core promises of AI is that the more it knows about a person, the better it will be able to assist them with tasks and make appropriate suggestions, which, if you'll believe the tech companies, requires apps and devices to…
items.x:
Ambi is releasing apps for iPhone, Mac, and Apple Watch that enables ambient capture
One of the core promises of AI is that the more it knows about a person, the better it will be able to assist them with tasks and make appropriate suggestions, which, if you’ll believe the tech companies, requires apps and devices to listen, watch or record users’ activity all the time and gather all possible context.
There’s obviously privacy and data security concerns with anything that’s collecting data about you continuously. But startups are building such apps undeterred anyway, arming themselves with the belief that the market for personalized assistance is big enough to swallow such concerns.
Former Plaud exec Peter Mo is building Ambi to do something similar. The app aims to provide real-time intelligence and insights to people by listening to them all the time.
The company said on Monday that it has raised $26 million across multiple funding rounds led by Luminous Ventures, which has backed companies like Meituan and Unitree Robotics, and Original Design Manufacturer (ODM) Huaqin.
Ambi is also releasing apps for iPhones, Macs and Apple Watch.

items.t: Amazon has over 1 million robot workers. What’s next for human employees?
items.d: The second-largest corporate employer has bet big on robot workers to scale.
items.x:
No organization in the world operates more robots than Amazon. The company already has more than 1 million robots working in warehouses around the clock to make tens of millions of same-day and one-day package deliveries happen on a daily basis—and Amazon is poised to significantly grow that robotic fleet in the coming years as it establishes new factories to churn out increasingly more capable robot workers.
Despite deploying so many robots, Amazon is also the second-largest corporate employer in the world, with more than 1.5 million full-time and part-time human workers, according to its 2025 annual report . Amazon executives say that the growing robot fleet has eased the burden on its human workforce by taking on the toughest fulfillment center tasks that carry the greatest risks of physical fatigue and injury.

items.t: Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
items.d: Meta is making up for lost time in the AI race. After launching Muse Spark, the first model from its revamped Superintelligence Labs division, and buzzy AI agent Muse, it's now launching two new models it claims can go toe-to-toe with the…
items.x:
Meta says the models compete with the industry’s best and will soon power its Muse agent.
Meta is making up for lost time in the AI race. After launching Muse Spark, the first model from its revamped Superintelligence Labs division, and buzzy AI agent Muse, it’s now launching two new models it claims can go toe-to-toe with the industry’s best.
The company says its new models can rival leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic, including GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.1, pointing to results from internal testing on several industry benchmarks. It’s unclear how they stack up against Google’s Gemini 4 Argon, whose capabilities are still coming into focus.
The launches are part of Meta’s aggressive push to reestablish itself as a major force in AI. The company has poured billions into talent and infrastructure and has been steadily expanding its AI lineup, including with image model Muse Image and a heavy focus on bringing useful AI agents to the masses through Muse.

items.t: Baidu World 2026 Set for November 12 in Beijing Under the Theme 'Next Act, Intelligent Organization'
items.d: Baidu will hold Baidu World 2026 on November 12 at the China National Convention Center Phase II in Beijing, with a theme centered on AI-driven organizational change. Tickets are on sale.
items.x:
Baidu will hold its annual Baidu World conference on November 12 at the China National Convention Center Phase II in Beijing, the company announced on October 12. Ticket sales have opened on the event's official website, IT Home reported.
This year's theme is "Next Act, Intelligent Organization." Baidu framed it as a callback to Baidu World 2016, where founder Robin Li said that the next act of the internet would be artificial intelligence. Ten years on, the company says the conference will turn its attention to how AI is reshaping the way organizations themselves are built and run.
Baidu has not yet disclosed which products it plans to launch. Its official preview promises a number of major announcements, with high-profile guests and enterprise AI products, along with 12 sub-forums on the intelligent organization theme, more than 30 open classes sharing hands-on AI technical experience, and a 6,000-square-meter exhibition area designed as an AI marketplace for visitors.
The emphasis on enterprise products and organizational change suggests the event will lean toward business customers rather than consumer gadgets, though the program has not been published in detail.

items.t: StepFun's Step 5 Preview Comes to Tencent WorkBuddy, Free to Use Exclusively Until October 25
items.d: StepFun's flagship Step 5 Preview model is now available inside Tencent's WorkBuddy office agent, with an exclusive free-use window running from October 12 to October 25.
items.x:
StepFun announced on October 12 that its Step 5 Preview model is now available in WorkBuddy, Tencent's AI-native office agent. From October 12 to October 25, Step 5 Preview can be used for free on WorkBuddy, an arrangement StepFun described as exclusive, according to IT Home.
The announcement covers access and timing only. StepFun did not say what happens to pricing in WorkBuddy after the two-week window closes, or whether the model will become a permanent option in the product.
For WorkBuddy users, the change adds another model choice inside an agent that already handles documents, spreadsheets, scheduling and other office tasks on desktop and mobile. For StepFun, it places its newest flagship directly in front of a large base of office users rather than only developers calling its API.
Step 5 Preview itself is not new. StepFun launched it on September 20 as a flagship aimed at AI coding, software engineering, professional knowledge work and finance, with a focus on agentic tasks in real-world settings. The model uses a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture with 600 billion total parameters and 27 billion active, supports a context window of 1 million tokens, and natively accepts text and visual input.

items.t: Huawei Noah's Ark Lab's Memento 3 Agent Clears All 25 ARC-AGI-3 Public Games With a Frozen Model
items.d: Memento 3, from Huawei Noah's Ark Lab, UCL and partners, writes its own rulebook and code world model. On a frozen Claude Opus 5 it scored 100 RHAE on the ARC-AGI-3 public set.
items.x:
Researchers from Huawei Noah's Ark Lab, University College London and other teams have released Memento 3, an agent system that cleared all 25 games and 183 levels in the public set of ARC-AGI-3, the interactive benchmark from the ARC Prize, according to QbitAI.
ARC-AGI-3 drops an agent into unfamiliar pixel-style games without telling it the rules, the goal or what its actions do. Memento 3 finished the public set in 7,518 actions against 17,135 for humans, about 44% of the human total, earning the maximum score of 100 on Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE). The previous best on the public set, independent developer Sergey Rodionov's baseline1, also cleared every game but scored 99 using 8,347 actions.
The result comes with two important caveats. The underlying model is not a Huawei model: Memento 3 runs on Claude Opus 5 at its highest reasoning setting, with no weight updates and no game-specific fine-tuning. And these are public games. A perfect public-set score does not show how the system would fare on hidden evaluation games, where generalization is actually tested. The same base model averages about 40.7 RHAE in the official ARC Prize harness, so the gain comes from the agent design around it.
That design is called Code as Model.

items.t: Huawei Details Xingji Positioning: Lane-Level Fixes in Tunnels, Floor Detection in Parking Garages
items.d: Huawei's new Xingji positioning stack fuses short-range chips, GNSS carrier phase, AI speed estimation and 3D road matching for tunnels, garages, malls, running tracks and ski slopes.
items.x:
Huawei has given the first detailed look at Xingji, a positioning technology it is debuting on the Mate 90 series and the WATCH GT Runner 2. Li Xiaolong, CTO of Huawei's Consumer Business Group and head of its hardware engineering and product development management department, presented the system at a Huawei device technology briefing on October 12, IT Home reported.
Li said conventional positioning no longer copes with the places people now navigate, from tunnels and elevated roads to underground garages, shopping malls, running tracks and ski slopes. Rather than one breakthrough, Xingji is a set of techniques matched to each of those scenarios.
On elevated roads, where drivers often miss lane changes without precise guidance, Huawei pairs a HiSilicon short-range chip with GNSS carrier phase measurement, which it says improves ranging accuracy more than tenfold and delivers sub-meter accuracy for lane-level navigation. Fusing RTK with AI-based pedestrian dead reckoning gives the Mate 90 series track-lane navigation on sports-ground running tracks.
Tunnels are the harder case because phones there usually rely on inertial sensors alone. Huawei combines AI speed estimation with geomagnetic matching, which it says is not limited by tunnel length or driving time.

Chinese AI infrastructure provider Infinigence AI has completed a RMB 2.3 billion Series C funding round, bringing its cumulative financing to RMB 4.3 billion, according to company materials provided on October 12. Founded in 2023, the company develops software and infrastructure that allow AI models to run efficiently across different chip platforms.
Its infrastructure platform connects 37,000 petaflops of computing capacity across 16 mainstream chip types and supports mixed-chip training using both Chinese and international processors. The company also provides AI model inference services and infrastructure solutions for enterprise AI agents, with applications in gaming, healthcare, legal services and energy.
Infinigence AI said its model-service platform’s daily token usage had increased 40-fold by July compared with December 2025. Its cross-cluster inference architecture reduced the time to generate the first token by 51.5% and cost per token by 37.5%, according to company figures. [TechNode reporting]

items.t: China Mobile Finishes Hohhot Computing Center Expansion, Taking Total Capacity to 20,100 PFLOPS
items.d: China Mobile's Hohhot expansion adds 120 MW of IT power. Once running, the site will offer 20,100 PFLOPS, 16,700 of it for AI, with 90% serving the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region.
items.x:
China Mobile has completed an expansion of its intelligent computing center in Hohhot, Inner Mongolia, according to Inner Mongolia Daily. The project, buildings B25 and B27 at China Mobile's Hohhot data center in the Horinger New Area, was built by China Construction Third Engineering Bureau and covers about 44,500 square meters with 120 MW of total IT power.
Once the expansion is in operation, the site's total computing capacity will reach 20,100 PFLOPS, of which 16,700 PFLOPS is intelligent computing for AI workloads. The report did not specify the numerical precision behind those figures. About 90% of the capacity is meant to serve the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, and green electricity accounts for 88% of supply.
The Hohhot campus is part of the national Eastern Data, Western Computing program, which moves computing loads from power-hungry eastern cities to western regions with cheaper renewable energy. It is a core node in China Mobile's 4+N+31+X computing network and a hub in the national integrated computing network.

items.t: Tencent Will Shut Down Its Yuanqi AI Agent Platform on November 9
items.d: Tencent Yuanqi stops creating new agents and API keys on October 29 and goes dark on November 9. Agents published to WeChat accounts will stop replying; data can be exported until January 9, 2027.
items.x:
Tencent is closing Yuanqi, the no-code platform it launched for building and distributing AI agents. In a notice dated October 8, the company said the platform will stop service on November 9, 2026, citing business adjustments. It gave no further reason.
The shutdown is staged. From October 29, users can no longer create new agents or obtain API keys, though existing agents keep working until the cutoff. On November 9, Tencent will turn off app access, data reads and writes, API calls and the developer console. Yuanqi agent pages will no longer display, and agents that were published from Yuanqi to other channels, including WeChat Official Accounts, Service Accounts and WeChat Customer Service, will stop answering users.
Tencent is advising users to export their data and migrate quickly. Until November 9, the platform's export tool lets them back up agent configurations, workflows and conversation records locally. After that, a transition period runs to January 9, 2027, during which users can still sign in to a data export console to download backups even though the rest of the platform is closed.

items.t: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
items.d: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
items.x:
Small AI models may be only months away from being able to self-replicate across cheap IoT devices like Android TV boxes, with no datacenter needed.
Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial IoT devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes. A replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off - though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days). Unlike non-AI malware, it could also figure out unfamiliar devices on its own. In our evals, a 9B model got inference running on 8 of the 9 hardware types we tested.
Models of 30B parameters and under can already complete many of the individual steps for replication today, though they make mistakes when composing them end to end. In our simplified evals, GLM-5.2 and stronger models are capable of end to end replication. If small models improve at their historical rate, they’ll match this capability level by the end of this year.

items.t: Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks
items.d: Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks
items.x:
Illicit distillation allows model developers to copy frontier AI capabilities without creating proportionally robust safeguards. Here, we describe how we’ve reduced the rate of distillation by more than 90%.
In recent months, we’ve made substantial progress on reducing the effectiveness of distillation attacks on Claude using new methods, as we outline in this blog. Early evidence suggests that these methods have reduced the amount of data harvested by distillers by around 90 to 99 percent.
Distillation attacks are covert, industrial-scale campaigns to extract the capabilities of one model and replicate them in another, without the authorization of the original model’s developers. They are often conducted using networks of fraudulent accounts. These attacks allow companies to mimic frontier capabilities for a fraction of the development time and cost. As we wrote in September, this method has been used extensively to help overseas AI laboratories keep pace with US companies.
We’re concerned about illicit distillation for two reasons. First, distillation enables companies to build models that approach the capability frontier, but which have, in practice, been released without proportionally robust safeguards.

| وقّعت إدارة المدينة الصناعية في حسياء بمحافظة حمص السورية وشركة «مدينة الابتكار والتكنولوجيا»، الأحد 11 أكتوبر 2026، مذكرة تفاهم لإنشاء مدينة متخصصة
وقّعت إدارة المدينة الصناعية في حسياء بمحافظة حمص السورية وشركة «مدينة الابتكار والتكنولوجيا»، الأحد 11 أكتوبر 2026، مذكرة تفاهم لإنشاء مدينة متخصصة بالصناعات التقنية، بهدف توطين التكنولوجيا ودعم التحول الرقمي، وفقًا لوكالة الأنباء السورية «سانا».
وأوضح أحمد كردي، المدير العام للمدن والمناطق الصناعية بوزارة الاقتصاد والصناعة، أن المذكرة تشمل مدينة صناعية تكنولوجية ومنطقة سكنية ببناها التحتية والفوقية لخدمة العاملين، مع استهداف استقطاب الكفاءات السورية وغيرها ونقل المعرفة.
وقال طلال زعيب، مدير عام المدينة الصناعية في حسياء، إن التصور يتضمن قسمًا صناعيًا بمساحة 990 هكتارًا وآخر سكنيًا بمساحة 550 هكتارًا. ويشمل القسم الصناعي مركزًا للبيانات تتجاوز مساحته 100 هكتار، بالتعاون مع وزارة الاتصالات وتقانة المعلومات، بينما تضم المنطقة السكنية معاهد وجامعات متخصصة ومرافق خدمية.
وتوقع ملهم راتب الدروبي، رئيس مجلس إدارة الشركة، أن يوفر المشروع نحو 52 ألف فرصة عمل وسكنًا لنحو 200 ألف نسمة، مع خدمات صحية وتعليمية وترفيهية وحاضنات للشركات الناشئة.

items.t: Can the AI industry persuade data center opponents by getting rid of NDAs?
items.d: On Equity, we debate the impact of data center moratoriums and whether the AI industry has a communication problem.
items.x:
On Equity, we debate the impact of data center moratoriums and whether the AI industry has a communication problem.
Amazon recently followed Microsoft’s lead and said it will no longer use nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) while negotiating with local governments over data centers.
On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Sean O’Kane, Rebeccan Bellan and I discussed Amazon’s announcement, which came in the middle of a longer blog post making the case that data centers are actually good for communities.
Rebecca was a bit skeptical that the recent spate of data center moratoriums will have a lasting effect, especially since the moratoriums only last for a year or two and “these data centers aren’t coming online for the next two, three, four, five years,” though I countered that data center backers definitely seem worried.
Sean, meanwhile, suggested that a big reason for the backlash is the industry’s poor communication.
“We’ve seen, through a lot of the controversy and backlash to AI and data centers, that the industry just does a really poor job explaining itself, and that they are obviously and constantly frustrated with the fact that most people can’t envision a world in which this stuff is useful for them,” he said.
Keep reading for a preview of our conversation…

items.t: CapCut, Tencent and Kuaishou Race to Build AI Tools for Interactive Film Games
items.d: ByteDance's CapCut team, Tencent and Kuaishou are all rolling out AI tools for branching, playable stories. Costs are falling, but scripts, hit titles and distribution remain open problems.
items.x:
Several of China's biggest internet companies are building AI tools for interactive film games, a genre of branching, playable video stories, in a bid to own the creator entry point for what could become a mass-produced content format, according to a Chinese media report published on October 11.
On September 20, ByteDance's video editor CapCut, in its China edition, unveiled ICG Studio, an AI interactive film game creation platform now in closed beta. Creators start from a story outline, then generate a script, persistent character, scene and prop assets, and storyboards. By chatting with an agent, they can branch the plot at any decision point and generate new storyboard shots, so characters and sets can be reused across storylines.
Tencent has four products across different teams. TDream, billed as AI engines for playable cinematic worlds, turns scripts into video and adds branching choices. LightSpeed Studios launched a creation platform in May that breaks interactive story production into six standardized steps for non-professional users. Project Craft, an AI game creation platform shown at Tencent's SPARK 2026 event, generates 2D and 3D game prototypes from text. DreamNow is a showcase and discovery platform for AI videos, images and interactive titles.

items.t: Ant Group's LingGuang 2.0 Enters Limited Beta as a Personal Agent With Long-Term Memory
items.d: Sources close to the project say Ant Group's LingGuang is testing a version that remembers users, pushes tasks forward on its own and calls Skills and MCP tools, with a full rollout due this month.
items.x:
Ant Group has quietly started a limited beta of a new version of LingGuang, its multimodal AI assistant, and is repositioning the app as a personal agent along the lines of Meta's Muse, according to Sina Tech, citing people close to the project. Ant has not made an official announcement.
Meta introduced Muse in September as a personal agent that steps into users' daily lives and keeps following up on the things they hand over. According to the sources, Ant began preparing a similar direction for LingGuang about six months ago, iterated through several internal versions and plans to open the new release to all users this month.
The core change, the sources said, is a shift in what LingGuang is for. The current app is built around chatting and generating content and small applications. The new version is designed as an AI-native personal agent with long-term memory that can move tasks forward on its own initiative rather than waiting for each prompt. It can also call Skills and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, which lets it send messages through Alibaba's workplace app DingTalk and operate smart home devices.
The beta use cases focus on long-running jobs with many moving parts that ordinary users struggle to keep track of.

items.t: Startup Led by Ex-Nvidia GPU Architect Designs Y10 Chip to Close Robot Control Loops in 1 ms
items.d: A Jiangsu chip startup founded by former Nvidia GPU architect Xu Feixiang is building Y10, a physical AI processor aiming for sub-millisecond closed-loop latency, with an FPGA platform due this year.
items.x:
A chip startup founded in 2025 by Xu Feixiang, a former GPU architect at Nvidia, is designing a processor built from scratch for physical AI, the robots and machines that sense, reason and act in the real world. Its first product, Y10, aims to cut the full perception, inference and action loop to under one millisecond, Xu told Chinese startup outlet Cyzone in an interview published October 10.
Xu argues that most robots today make do with CPUs, GPUs and autonomous-driving chips. GPUs are built for throughput on large language models, he said, not for the continuous loop in which a robot senses its surroundings, acts and then adjusts at high frequency based on feedback. For physical AI, the useful measure is how long the whole loop takes and what it costs in power and money, not just peak TOPS. He estimates that chip architecture accounts for about 70% of how usable a parallel processor is, and software for 30%.
Rather than a fixed-function ASIC, Y10 is a general-purpose processor driven by a custom, highly programmable instruction set, so it can keep up as robot models change. According to earlier company material, the design is based on an architecture it calls SomaArch.

items.t: DeepSeek Harness v0.2.1-alpha.2 Pre-Release Adds Reasoning Translation and Git Worktrees
items.d: DeepSeek's open-source agent runtime adds experimental reasoning translation and Git Worktrees plugins, a working_directory tool, SDK session-directory APIs and an SSH helper.
items.x:
DeepSeek has published DeepSeek Harness v0.2.1-alpha.2, a new pre-release of its open-source agent runtime. The build went up on the project's official GitHub page on the evening of October 9 Beijing time, six days after v0.2.1-alpha.1, and is still marked Pre-release rather than a stable version.
The headline addition is an experimental plugin that machine-translates a model's reasoning output. Users switch it on from the Plugins page and choose Bing, Google or paid DeepSeek Flash as the translation provider. A second experimental plugin adds Git Worktrees, letting an agent create and move into a separate Git checkout so parallel work does not collide in one working copy. Experimental plugins also get new session state-record APIs for writing and reading their own records.
Several changes target developers building on the runtime. A new working_directory tool lets the agent read and change the session's working directory, and the TypeScript and Python SDKs gain matching APIs. Global instructions can now be loaded from an AGENTS.md file in a shared agents directory, set through the DSH_AGENTS_HOME variable.

items.t: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’
items.d: In a Saturday morning post, Microsoft's CEO wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI.
items.x:
In a Saturday morning post, Microsoft's CEO wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI.
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is the latest tech executive to offer lengthy thoughts on how AI safety might be improved.
In a Saturday morning post on X, Nadella wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI.
“We can’t treat Super Intelligence as a set of nested black boxes and simply accept or reject its recommendations, answers, and actions,” Nadella wrote, using the Trump administration’s preferred term for AI.
As outlined by Nadella, this approach “means separating the model from the harness that orchestrates its work,” as well as “externalizing controls and safeguards.” He also called for “every meaningful model action” to be documented with “tamper-proof human readable evidence,” and for systems where “an authorized person” always has the ability “to pause or shut down a model mid-task.”
“We must assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start,” he said.

items.t: Apple discloses deal to hire team and license tech from personalized podcast startup Huxe
items.d: Is Apple hoping to get into the AI-generated podcast business?
items.x:
Is Apple hoping to get into the AI-generated podcast business?
Apple revealed in a regulatory filing that it has reached an agreement to bring on team members and technology from personalized audio startup Huxe, in what’s commonly known as a reverse acqui-hire deal.
As first reported in MacRumors, Apple disclosed to the European Commission that it has agreed to make employment offers to “certain employees of Huxe AI,” and to “receive a non-exclusive license to Huxe’s intellectual property rights.”
Reverse acqui-hires emerged in recent years as a way for larger companies to hire key team members and license technology from startups without acquiring the startups outright — presumably allowing them to build up AI talent and tech without drawing as much antitrust scrutiny. (Confusingly, these deals have both been referred to as “reverse acqui-hires” and as plain old “acqui-hires.”)
In the case of Huxe, the startup was founded by developers who’d previously worked on the AI-generated podcast features in NotebookLM (recently renamed Gemini Notebook).

items.t: As AI mass-produces historical dramas in China, where are the boundaries?
items.d: In 2026, AI is changing how historical dramas are produced in China. In the past, dramas featuring ancient battles, palace architecture and elaborate costumes often required large budgets and professional production teams. Today, AI…
items.x:
In 2026, AI is changing how historical dramas are produced in China. In the past, dramas featuring ancient battles, palace architecture and elaborate costumes often required large budgets and professional production teams.
Today, AI generation and virtual compositing tools are making it possible for smaller teams and even individual creators to produce historical scenes that were once difficult to realize. As production barriers fall, the volume of content is growing rapidly.
But as AI makes it possible to generate historical figures, battle scenes and depictions of ancient societies at scale, an important question emerges: when seemingly realistic historical narratives can be produced at low cost and in large quantities, how do we distinguish artistic interpretation from historical distortion?

items.t: Striding AI Unveils H1 and C1 Robots for 24/7 Convenience Stores, Targets 2027 Service Launch
items.d: Striding AI showed a humanoid H1, a narrow wheeled-arm C1 and an M1 fleet platform for round-the-clock convenience stores, saying they need no shelf or layout changes.
items.x:
Striding AI, a Beijing physical AI startup, has unveiled a robot system for convenience stores that run around the clock. The company showed it on October 8 at the 22nd Asia-Pacific Retailers Convention and Exhibition (APRCE 2026), according to a company release carried by QbitAI.
The system has three parts. H1 is a bipedal humanoid designed for spaces where customers move around. It speaks more than 20 languages, can show 45 facial expressions and 36 gestures, and offers an open API for custom development. C1 is a wheeled robot with arms for narrow aisles. It runs on a slim omnidirectional base, reaches from about 100 mm to more than 1,750 mm high, and handles moving goods, restocking shelves and loading. Striding AI says C1 senses nearby shoppers with fused sensors, stops within 10 cm of an obstacle in an emergency, and carries front and rear depth cameras plus 360-degree vision. M1 is the management platform that assigns tasks, tracks status and lets staff take over.
The company says the setup needs no changes to store shelves or walkways, which it calls zero retrofit. It wants the robots to take on repetitive and overnight work such as restocking, stock checks and patrols, so staff can focus on customers.

items.t: Alibaba's Qoder Adds Fast Mode With 3-Second First Responses and Lower Credit Use
items.d: Alibaba's Qoder coding agent has launched a Fast tier that answers in about three seconds at 0.8x credits, replacing the Performance tier on its international edition.
items.x:
Alibaba's AI coding agent Qoder has added a Fast mode built for everyday tasks that need quick turnaround. The company said on October 10 that the new tier is live first in the Qoder desktop app, version 0.4.4 and later, for both individual and enterprise users, on the China and international editions at the same time, IT Home reported.
Qoder lists Fast with a first response time of about three seconds, high output quality and a credit rate of 0.8x. On the China edition, Fast is a new tier added alongside the existing options. On the international edition, it replaces the previous Performance tier rather than sitting next to it.
For international users, the company says the change brings a faster and cheaper tier with no loss in quality. First response time falls from about eight seconds to three, and the credit rate drops from 1.1x to 0.8x, roughly 27% less. Qoder says output quality is the same as Performance, and users on the old tier are moved over automatically with nothing to change on their side.
Qoder also published first-response times for its other tiers. By its own measurements, Fast at three seconds compares with 7.9 seconds for Performance on the international edition, 9.8 seconds for Auto and 13 seconds for Ultimate on the international edition.
